left untouched (its competencies prop is already scoped upstream and may
carry an admin override). Also drops the optimistic "about 12-15 minutes"
copy; the statement count now reflects the scoped set.

Verified: selecting the SDAIA HR role drops Part 1 from 164 to 48 statements.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Harden Persona scoping + seed SDAIA HR role profile
entries.plain: Persona fit scores are now calculated consistently on screen and in downloadable reports, and candidates cannot manipulate assessment scope through technical workarounds.
entries.explanation:
Review fixes for the SD-1 scoping build:
- On-screen hiring fit now computes over the role competencies actually
  served (filter to measured), mirroring the PDF route - a scoped run no
  longer understates fit on screen or diverges from the downloaded PDF.
- saveBehavioralAnswers enforces the pinned competency scope server-side:
  out-of-scope answers are dropped at the write path, so a crafted call
  can't inject competencies and widen a pinned assessment (the UI filter
  alone was not load-bearing).
- Robust undefined-column detection (42703 read + PGRST204 write) drives
  the 00123/00110 strip-and-retry fallbacks, replacing message regexes
  that missed the PostgREST write-path error shape.

Plus migration 00124: a starter "SDAIA - HR / Talent Acquisition
Specialist" role profile (12 framework competencies, weighted +
prioritised + per-competency targets) so the Persona hiring picker has
a credible SDAIA-relevant target role for the TA pilot.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Add admin-pinned competency scoping to Persona vouchers (SD-1)
entries.plain: Persona assessment links now lock in the skills to be tested and the purpose (hiring or development) at the time of issuance, so candidates cannot change the scope.
entries.explanation:
A Persona voucher now pins the assessment config at issuance: purpose
(hiring/development), a target role profile, and the competency scope.
The candidate redeems and just takes the pre-configured test - they
cannot change or widen it (scope is derived server-side from the
voucher, never trusted from the client). The runner serves only the
scoped competencies' items (full bank ~164; a subset ~4 x N), and the
hiring fit report computes over the served competencies only.

- Migration 00123: persona_vouchers.purpose + target_role_profile_id +
  scoped_competency_ids; behavioral_assessment_sessions.scoped_competency_ids
- vouchers lib/action: persist scope, tolerant of 00123 absent; a hiring
  voucher requires a target role (server-guarded)
- voucher issuance UI: purpose toggle + role picker (pre-fills the role's
  competencies) + per-cluster competency picker with Full-profile/Clear
- take page + runner: filter served competencies; lock the picker when
  pinned (read-only "Assessing for <role>")
- startPersonaAction: derive + override scope from the voucher server-side
- report: fit over measured role competencies only (no zero for unserved)

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Persona: randomized + section-hidden flow, ipsative items, purpose-by-pillar
entries.plain: Persona questions now appear in random order with section labels hidden to reduce bias, and questions are shuffled differently for hiring versus development purposes.
entries.explanation:
Reworks the Persona (behavioural self-assessment) product surface per the
talent-acquisition vs talent-development split:

- Hide sections + randomize. Likert statements now present in a seeded-random
  flat order with cluster/section labels hidden (reduces section priming +
  ordering effects). The seed is stored on the session so a report can
  reconstruct exactly what the taker saw. Paginated 12/page.
- Two item types. Adds an IPSATIVE forced-choice section ("most / least like
  me" blocks of four, one forward statement per competency) alongside the
  NORMATIVE Likert section. Forced-choice maps to a 1-5 contribution
  (most=5, least=1, mid=3) and flows through the same per-competency rollup,
  so no scoring-engine change is needed; item_type/answer_data are stored for
  audit + reproducibility.
- Purpose-by-pillar. The intro asks what the run is for:
  - Hiring/selection -> a role FIT SCORE (weighted-gap vs a target role
    profile) + biggest gaps, with the screening-not-decision guardrail.
  - Development -> per-competency explanation + suggestions (band narrative +
    development tips on the rows that need them).
- Report. Persona PDF now carries competency DEFINITIONS, per-competency band
  narrative, development suggestions, and a hiring fit panel.

New pure libs: persona-format.ts (seeded shuffle, flatten, forced-choice
blocks), persona-fit.ts (weighted fit), persona-roles.ts (role loader).
Migration 00110 (write-only; user applies): behavioral_assessment_sessions +=
purpose/target_role_profile_id/randomization_seed; responses += item_type/
answer_data. All paths tolerant of 00110 not being applied (strip-and-retry).
The candidate-bound readiness "self" feed is intentionally unchanged.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Fix clipboard crash on Copy (NotAllowedError) + add fallback
entries.plain: The copy-link button on ARC assessment links no longer crashes in certain browsers or restricted environments and now falls back to alternative copy methods.
entries.explanation:
The ARC vouchers "Copy links" button fired navigator.clipboard.writeText
without awaiting/catching, so a denied write (e.g. an iframe lacking
clipboard-write permission, like the dev preview) surfaced as an
unhandled runtime error. Add a shared copyToClipboard() helper
(src/lib/utils/clipboard.ts): Clipboard API first, then a legacy
execCommand fallback that works in those contexts, throwing only if both
fail. Wire it into all four voucher screens (ARC fix + Cognitive/Fluent/
Persona). Verified: Copy no longer crashes and shows the copied state.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Fix React hydration mismatches from locale date/number formatting
entries.plain: Date and number formatting across assessment voucher pages now displays consistently in all browsers, eliminating display mismatches.
entries.explanation:
toLocaleDateString()/toLocaleString() with no fixed locale/timezone
render differently on the server vs the browser ("17/06/2026" vs
"6/17/2026"), tripping "Text content did not match" in client
components. Add a shared deterministic UTC formatter
(src/lib/utils/format-date.ts) and apply it across the four voucher
screens (ARC/Cognitive/Fluent/Persona), the notification bell, and the
Reflect IDP editor; pin the Pre-Hire client-report date to UTC and the
Evidence Map number format to en-US. (Washup uses a post-mount event
time, not SSR, so it's untouched.)

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Admin nav: group self-serve instruments; expose retention surfaces
entries.plain: The admin menu now groups self-serve assessments (Cognitive, Persona, Fluent) and Pre-Hire into expandable sections showing all management options, improving navigation.
entries.explanation:
Promotes the self-serve instruments (Cognitive, Persona, Fluent) and
Pre-Hire from single sidebar links to expandable groups listing their
management surfaces (Overview / Cohort / Vouchers / Calibration /
Retention), matching the Technical + Assessment Center pattern. Closes
the Cognitive admin-console discoverability gap and makes the new
retention pages reachable from the sidebar. Adds shared svc* i18n keys
(EN/AR).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Persona to ARC bar: cohort report + retention admin
entries.plain: Persona now includes an organization-wide cohort report showing skill distributions and a data retention tool for purging old assessments after 24 months.
entries.explanation:
- Org-scoped cohort report at /ac/persona/cohort (overall self-rating +
  band distribution across the 38 competencies, per-run report links,
  client filter; standalone candidate_id-null runs only).
- Retention admin at /ac/persona/retention (24-month purge of standalone
  behavioral_assessment_sessions, typed confirmation, admin-gated;
  candidate-bound readiness sessions untouched).
- Cohort + Retention nav links on the Persona runner.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Persona: standalone voucher model
entries.plain: Persona now has its own independent voucher system, so admins can issue assessment links directly and track redemptions the same way as other platforms.
entries.explanation:
Give the Persona behavioural self-assessment its own independent voucher
system (mirrors Fluent/Cognitive):
- persona_vouchers + redemptions + claim RPC (migration 00106);
  behavioral_assessment_sessions gains organization_id + voucher_redemption_id
- admin console /ac/persona/vouchers; public redeem /ac/persona/redeem ->
  token runner /ac/persona/take/[token]; startPersonaAction stamps the session
  with the client org on a voucher run (best-effort, non-voucher path unchanged)
- middleware bypass for the delegate paths. Tolerant; inert until 00106 applied.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Refresh PENDING-ACTIONS: record 2026-06-16 work + new open items
entries.plain: Internal tracking updated to reflect recently completed work and pending tasks.
entries.explanation:
- Date bumped to 2026-06-16.
- New section G logs this session's shipped work (auth-doc fix, Persona
  scoping + bands, 9th cluster 00100, Succession Readiness combined wiring

- Added open items: create ahmad.rashid admin, rotate the demo credential,

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Scope Persona to agreed competencies + add interpretation bands
entries.plain: Persona assessments now evaluate only the competencies your organization agreed to assess for each role, making results more focused and relevant to your hiring needs.
entries.explanation:
- Candidate-bound Persona now evaluates only the engagement's agreed
  competencies (engagement_competencies), falling back to the full 38 when
  none are selected. The master framework is unchanged; each engagement
  draws its agreed subset. Standalone /ac/persona stays full-framework.
- Add a shared 5-band interpretation guide (Exceptional -> Critical Gap,
  bilingual) on the candidate submit screen, the standalone result, and the
  Persona PDF.

services.label: AR Compass (ARC)
services.blurb: AI Readiness Compass - organisation + individual readiness.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC consolidation: bring Division and Enterprise to the unit-report standard
entries.plain: Division and enterprise reports now match the visual quality and detail of department reports instead of appearing as bare summaries.
entries.explanation:
Client instruction (2026-09-02): the department and individual reports
are detailed, colourful and diagrammed; the division and enterprise
consolidations were five and six light pages. They are now built to the
same standard, and every page is generated from data - nothing is
hand-tailored, and sections without data behind them do not render.

Structure (Division 16 pages, Enterprise 17, both EN and AR):
- Executive summary with stat tiles, gauge, narrative and the same
  "at or approaching target / requiring focus" panels as the unit report.
- "Reading this report": the maturity ladder from ARA_MATURITY_LEVELS,
  the two consolidation findings (shared gap, uneven pillar) with the
  counts this run produced, and a contents list.
- Units ranked as a bar chart plus table with a data-driven callout;
  under an enterprise, a division drill-down page with a per-division
  "who carries, who drags" panel.
- Units-by-pillar matrix with a mean row; a multi-unit radar; a spread
  chart (min-max range per pillar, mean marker, colour by finding).
- An agenda matrix: X is categorical by the report's own finding (some
  unit at 4.00 versus shared gap), Y is spread against the uneven
  threshold; quadrants Central programme / Lift the rest / Move practice
  / Sustain. The first cut split X on the mean (< 3.00) and so placed
  four shared gaps under "Sustain" while the text called them central -
  caught on the rendered page, now derived from sharedGap + spread.
- One deep-dive page per pillar in scope: tiles, unit bars, narrative,
  and three consolidation-level actions chosen by quadrant with the
  strongest / weakest unit names substituted (bilingual copy in
  rollup-copy.ts).
- Workforce readiness across units when any department ran the
  individual layer: four-factor bars, per-unit table, and a
  people-versus-systems reading.
- A twelve-month roadmap generated from the quadrants (owners, central
  standards, playbooks, transfers, uncovered pillars, re-measure),
  capped so it always fits its page.
- VIFM training pooled across the units' own recommendations, ranked
  by how many units the same programme serves.
- Next steps + Phase 2, and a method appendix from consolidationFactRows.

Also fixed while reading the render: SVG text anchors under an inherited
rtl direction clipped every Arabic chart label to its last glyph (charts
now sit in dir="ltr" wrappers); the guided-demo launcher printed onto the
PDF cover (now no-print); "4 of 4 divisions ran the individual layer"
counted departments as divisions. Samples landing updated to the new
page counts.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Admin sidebar: "Sample reports" link to the client sample set
entries.plain: Staff can now reach sample reports from the admin sidebar instead of having to type in the URL manually.
entries.explanation:
/samples is the one page business development shares with a prospect
(the live-rendered ARC deliverables plus the interactive dashboard), but
it was reachable only by typing the URL. Listed under Platform, beside
Licensed Preview, so staff can open it from the left panel.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: live interactive dashboard at every level, with optional segments
entries.plain: The interactive dashboard now shows real assessment data at all organizational levels with optional drill-down by team segments.
entries.explanation:
The /samples/arc-dashboard page was a static August mock-up: an embedded
JSON tree with invented constructs (awareness / adoption / readiness) and
demographics nobody had ever been asked. Replace it with the shipped
dashboard rendered from the real engine, and make the same dashboard
openable on any client assessment.

- src/lib/ara/dashboard-tree.ts: buildDashboardTree(rootId) walks
  computeUnitRollup (00200 links, two-level pooling) for divisions and
  the enterprise, a leaf's own ara_pillar_scores for departments, and
  computeWorkforceReadiness for the people beneath each leaf. One tree,
  organisation -> division -> department -> person, every number the one
  the PDF reports print.
- src/components/ara/arc-dashboard.tsx: bilingual EN/AR drill-down with
  breadcrumbs, four tiles, and tabs (Overview, Units by pillar, People,
  Segments, Training) that appear only when there is data behind them.
- Mount points: /ara/consultant/assessments/[id]/dashboard (ownership-
  gated like report and rollup, PDF links per node, "Dashboard" button on
  the assessment page) and the public /samples/arc-dashboard on the Ufuq
  enterprise fixture. Landing page card and copy updated.
- Segments are OPTIONAL (client decision 2026-09-02): migration 00202
  adds ara_respondents.demographics jsonb; the vocabulary (grade, tenure,
  gender, nationality as national vs expatriate) lives in
  src/lib/constants/ara-demographics.ts; individual-layer respondents get
  an "About you (optional)" card with "Prefer not to say" on every
  question; the dashboard shows aggregates only, drops any group under
  three people, and says why the tab is missing.
- recommendCoursesForAraAssessment accepts an optional client so the
  public page can read via the service role.
- Fix found while verifying: selecting a column the joined table lacks
  made PostgREST return null silently and the page 404'd; the adapter
  now logs the root select error.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC samples: "the four never disagree" - the copy still counted three
entries.plain: Sample report text now correctly refers to four reports instead of three after enterprise reports were added.
entries.explanation:
Caught reading the rendered page: the closing sentence of "How the four fit
together" still said "the three never disagree" from before the enterprise
document was added.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC samples: list the interactive dashboard on the samples page
entries.plain: The interactive dashboard now has its own card on the samples page to make it easy to find and clearly mark it as illustrative.
entries.explanation:
Client instruction (2026-09-02). The dashboard gets its own card beneath the
four documents rather than a fifth slot in their grid: those four are
generated live through the client code path and the page says so; the
dashboard is an illustrative preview of the drill-down on sample data with a
construct model that differs from the shipped instrument, and its card says
that too. One link, the page's own EN/AR toggle.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC samples: the illustrative note the previous commit claimed but did not add
entries.plain: An explanatory note now correctly appears on the dashboard page to clarify it shows sample data with illustrative labels.
entries.explanation:
05feee9 restored the dashboard and its message described a bilingual note under
the toolbar; the insertion had failed silently (the page has no .toolbar - its
header is <header class="top"> and its language toggle is setLang()), so the
page went out without it. The note is now inserted after the header and
follows the page's own language switch. It says the dashboard is an
illustrative preview of the drill-down on sample data, that its construct
labels are illustrative, that the shipped instrument scores eight
organisational pillars and four individual factors, and points to /samples for
the live reports.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC samples: reactivate the interactive organisational dashboard
entries.plain: The interactive organizational dashboard is back on the samples page with a note explaining it uses sample data.
entries.explanation:
Client instruction (2026-09-02): the interactive dashboard at
/samples/arc-dashboard is wanted back at its original link. Restored as it
was from 0d75b47 (the last commit before it was retired).

One addition, so the page cannot sell a model the product does not measure: a
bilingual note under the toolbar stating that the dashboard is an illustrative
preview of the drill-down experience on sample data, that its construct labels
(AI Awareness / Adoption / Readiness) are illustrative, that the shipped
instrument scores eight organisational pillars and four individual factors,
and pointing to /samples for the live reports.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: enterprise consolidation - two-level rollup with division drill-down
entries.plain: Enterprise reports now show division scores pooled from their departments so you can compare divisions on equal terms.
entries.explanation:
Client decision (2026-09-02): under per-unit pricing an Enterprise is "its
divisions' units plus an organisation-level consolidation", so the deliverable
the Enterprise price attaches to has to exist before it is quoted.

ENGINE (src/lib/ara/unit-rollup.ts): a child with no scores of its own that is
itself a rollup - a division inside an enterprise - now has its pillar scores
POOLED from its departments, respondent-weighted (or equal-weighted), so an
enterprise compares divisions on the same 1.00-5.00 scale a division compares
departments. Two levels deep at most (Enterprise -> Division -> Department;
the guard also stops a mis-linked cycle). RollupUnit gains `children` and
`pooled`; totalRespondents counts leaves once, never a pooled unit twice.

REPORT: the ranked table marks pooled units "(N departments)", and a
"Departments within each division" drill-down sits directly beneath it - a
division can look average while one department inside it is well ahead and
another well behind, and that is where a board sees it. Bilingual. The first
cut put the drill-down on its own page and left the ranking on a sheet
nine-tenths empty; merged.

SAMPLE: /samples/arc-enterprise, live-rendered from the fixture, which gained
an Enterprise over two divisions - Corporate Services (Finance, HR) and
Operations (Digital Services, Customer Care), 39 respondents. The landing page
becomes four documents. Verified: 5 pages EN / 5 AR, 817 shaped Arabic
characters, no overlay; Operations reads 3.20 while its drill-down shows
Digital Services 3.66 and Customer Care 2.68 - exactly the finding the level
exists to expose.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: price labels follow the per-unit model
entries.plain: ARC pricing now clearly states the per-unit model - first department free, additional departments and consolidations charged separately.
entries.explanation:
Client decision (2026-09-02): ARC is priced per unit assessed plus a
consolidation fee. The first department stays complimentary - it is the land;
every further department is one unit at one price; a division is N units plus
the cross-unit consolidation; an enterprise is its divisions' units plus the
organisation-level consolidation. Flat named tiers were rejected because a
three-department and a nine-department division would have cost the same.

Stage definitions now say so ("First department complimentary" / "Per
department assessed + consolidation" / "Per unit assessed + consolidation",
EN + AR), and the engagement page's summary strip reads the label from the
constant instead of restating "Complimentary / Fee-based" by hand. The
proposals module already quotes ARC "per business unit"; the consolidation is
its own engagement line.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: link the engagement page to the sample reports
entries.plain: The ARC engagement page now links to sample reports so prospects can see what each pricing tier delivers before exploring training.
entries.explanation:
/ara/engage explains the stages; /samples shows what each stage delivers. A
prospect who has just read the tiers wants to see the output before the
training catalogue, so the samples bridge sits ahead of the catalogue bridge.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: samples landing page, and a link to every employee's individual report
entries.plain: A new samples landing page lets prospects explore all four ARC reports in one place, and individual reports are now directly accessible.
entries.explanation:
TWO THINGS, ONE THEME - what exists must be reachable.

1. /samples - one public page for business development to share instead of
   six PDF links. Frames the three deliverables as one engagement journey
   (department report -> division consolidation -> individual report), with
   English and Arabic links to each live render, and says plainly that the
   organisation is fictional and every document is generated through the
   client code path. Client decision 2026-09-02.

2. Individual reports inside a department engagement were generated but
   reachable from NOWHERE. The assessment page's respondents tab linked only
   to each person's survey; the consultant dashboard's personal-activity
   panel lists standalone snapshots only (engagement_stage = individual). A
   consultant would have had to hand-build /ara/personal/results/<token>.
   The client asked "where are the individual reports" and that was the
   honest answer. Now: the respondents tab shows "Individual report" + EN/AR
   PDF for every completed respondent when the individual layer is on, and
   the Phase 2 workforce table carries the same links per person (its rows
   come from the rollup by respondent id, so the token is resolved through
   the respondents list).

Verified on the Ufuq HR fixture: 12 report links and 12 PDF links on each of
the two tabs, one per completed respondent. Note for anyone testing Radix
tabs headlessly: a synthetic element.click() does not switch the panel -
the first two checks counted zero for that reason - use real mouse events.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC samples: resolve the render origin the way the PDF routes do
entries.plain: Fixed a technical error that caused AR Compass department and division reports to crash on our live system - they now render correctly like individual reports do.
entries.explanation:
On production the department and division samples failed in under a second
with a bare 500 while the individual report (which renders from a string, no
navigation) worked. The two failing routes built Chromium's target from
request.url; behind Render's proxy that is the container-internal address
(https on localhost), which Chromium cannot connect to, so page.goto threw
before any page loaded. The org PDF routes have always gone through
selfOrigin() for exactly this - it maps https://localhost back to http. The
sample routes now do the same. Verified locally; production re-verified after
deploy.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: Arabic edition of the division consolidation
entries.plain: Added Arabic language support to the division consolidation report so Saudi government leaders can read their results in Arabic.
entries.explanation:
Client decision (2026-09-02): the division consolidation was the only
deliverable without an Arabic edition, and the division head of a Saudi
government client is exactly who reads it - so Arabic comes before the sample
set goes to any prospect, not after.

- The rollup page takes ?lang=ar: RTL, every label and narrative sentence in
  Arabic, pillar / maturity-level / overall-band / stage names read from the
  constants' Arabic fields (never restated), the organisation's Arabic name
  when it has one, Noto Naskh loaded for shaping. Western digits, as in the
  other Arabic reports.
- Unit names in Arabic: computeUnitRollup now carries scope_label_ar (falling
  back to the English label), and the page maps the spreads' strongest /
  weakest names back through the unit list so tables and narrative agree.
- MaturityGauge takes a lang and shows the band's Arabic label.
- /api/ara/reports/[id]/rollup/pdf accepts ?language=en|ar; the page's toolbar
  offers both downloads; /samples/arc-division accepts ?lang=ar again, for real
  this time.

Caught by reading the rendered Arabic page as an image, not by tests: the
Next.js dev error overlay ("2 errors") had been printed INTO the PDF. The
cause was a hydration mismatch - a <style> element with a quoted string child
is HTML-escaped by the server ("'") and not by the client. Switched to
dangerouslySetInnerHTML; both languages now render with zero console errors.

Verified through the live sample route: EN 5 pages / AR 5 pages, 656 shaped
Arabic characters, no replacement glyphs, no overlay, unit names and pillar
names in Arabic, RTL matrix and tables.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC samples: sell what we ship - three live-rendered deliverables, two stale pages retired
entries.plain: Updated public samples to show the three real reports clients actually receive, generated through the same process as paid engagements.
entries.explanation:
Client decision (2026-09-02): the public samples are the three deliverables a
client actually receives, each generated through the same code path as a
paying client's, for the sandbox fixture "Ufuq Digital Authority" (Corporate
Services division over Human Resources and Finance, 22 respondents, deep-dive
with the individual layer on).

  /samples/arc-department  - the department report (HR), ?lang=ar
  /samples/arc-division    - the division consolidation (English only)
  /samples/arc-report      - the individual report (Abdullah Alanazi), ?lang=ar

RETIRED: /samples/arc-dashboard (an org-wide drill-down on the three
constructs the product never measured) and /samples/arc-recommendation (an
"optimisation" note recommending a 36-item form the product does not offer;
the real answer is the standard 49/71/99 forms and custom scope). Both were
hand-authored in August for BD; a prospect could be sold something the product
does not produce.

MIDDLEWARE: a narrow bypass so a cookieless internal render can reach
/ara/consultant/assessments/<uuid>/report|rollup. The page and the consultant
layout already honoured the server-only x-ara-internal header
(isInternalAraRender), but middleware ran first and bounced Chromium to
/login - the first attempt at these samples shipped a print of the login page,
caught by the wrong_page trap. Matches only those two page paths, only with
the exact secret, compared in constant time (inlined: Edge has no
node:crypto). Same trust boundary as the existing cron endpoints.

The division sample deliberately accepts no ?lang: the rollup page has no
Arabic edition yet, and the first cut returned English for ?lang=ar with
identical bytes - exactly the kind of mismatch these samples exist to end.

Dev note: rendering the org-level samples locally needs CRON_SECRET in
.env.local (gitignored; production already has it).

Verified through the live routes: department 22 pages incl. the Workforce
AI Readiness section, division 5 pages with units-by-pillar and shared-vs-
uneven analysis, neither landing on the login page.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: one personal-report renderer for EN and AR, and a sample that is a real render
entries.plain: Personal reports now use the same renderer for English and Arabic, and the sample report matches what clients truly receive instead of showing a different assessment model.
entries.explanation:
Ahmad compared the live Personal Snapshot PDF against the "Detailed
Individual Report" sample and asked what the difference was. The honest
answer was that the sample was a hand-authored HTML page (August, for BD)
built on a three-construct model - AI Awareness / Adoption / Readiness with
nine sub-dimensions - that the product has never measured. A prospect buying
off it would have received a different instrument.

WHAT CHANGED
- ONE renderer, src/lib/reports/personal-report-html.ts, for both languages,
  printed through Chromium like every organisational report. Replaces the
  React-PDF English renderer and the Puppeteer Arabic one, which had drifted
  apart (percentiles and cohort deltas reached the screen but neither PDF).
  Their bilingual copy - the 12 stage x factor blurbs, next-steps, legends -
  moved verbatim into personal-report-copy.ts so the two languages can no
  longer fork.
- src/lib/reports/personal-report-build.ts assembles the data and is shared
  by every caller: the token route and the public sample. Authorisation stays
  with the routes; the builder trusts the token it is handed.
- The sample's LAYOUT was kept, as the client asked - executive summary,
  factor cards with sub-scores, strengths against priorities, 30/60/90,
  comparison bars, training, manager guide - and re-based on the four factors
  the instrument measures. Sub-scores are the real coded split per factor
  (self-rated Likert items vs the scenario/knowledge items the deep-dive
  adds), not invented sub-dimensions. The comparison rows are the unit cohort
  (computeWorkforceReadiness) and the organisation pooled across its
  individual-layer assessments; a standalone snapshot says it has no cohort
  rather than faking one.
- /samples/arc-report now serves the REAL report for a sandbox fixture
  (Abdullah Alanazi, Ufuq Digital Authority, HR + Finance departments under
  Corporate Services, 22 respondents) inline as a PDF, ?lang=ar for Arabic.
  Whatever the product produces is what the prospect opens. The static HTML
  and its generator are gone.

READING THE RENDER AS A CLIENT WOULD, THEN FIXING WHAT IT SHOWED
- "sits below the unit average" beside two numbers that both printed 3.5:
  the comparison block now uses two decimals (3.45 vs 3.55).
- The 30/60/90 plan repeated the priority actions verbatim; it is now a
  progression - start priority 1's first step, keep it and add priority 2,
  then the stage's stretch move and a re-measure.
- The executive summary called the weakest factor "the priority" while the
  ordered list put it second (foundation-first sequencing is deliberate);
  it now says "carries the largest gap" and lets the list own "priority".
- A course tagged to two competencies of one factor listed the factor twice;
  drivers are deduplicated at their strongest relevance. Course levels were
  raw enums ("advanced"); title-cased.
- A side-by-side strengths/priorities grid left most of a page blank when
  priorities ran long; strengths are now a band and priorities two-up.
  Comparison box and fact sheet no longer split across a page break.

Verified through the live route: EN 4 pages, AR 4 pages, 1,813 shaped Arabic
characters and zero replacement glyphs, every page inspected as an image.
Also removed scripts/verify-ar-pdf-html.ts, which only existed to exercise
the deleted Arabic renderer.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: capture the division at creation, so a rollup is possible later
entries.plain: System now records which division a department belongs to when created, making it possible to build division-level reports later.
entries.explanation:
The commercial sequence runs opposite to the data model. 00200 gave us
parent_assessment_id, but that link can only be made once a rollup EXISTS. What
actually happens is:

  1. A client buys ONE department assessment. Vouchers issued, report lands.
  2. They like it: "do another department in the same division, and give us a
     division report."
  3. Nobody recorded which division the first department belonged to - it was
     never asked. Grouping becomes archaeology, and the further apart the two
     sittings, the worse it gets.

MIGRATION 00201 (applied): ara_assessments.parent_unit_label - the unit ABOVE
this one. Deliberately a LABEL, not a foreign key: at the moment it is captured
the parent does not exist as a row, and forcing one would mean creating an empty
division assessment nobody ordered. parent_assessment_id stays the authoritative
link once a rollup is built; this is how you FIND the units to link.

Named parent_unit_label rather than division_label because the same need exists
one level up - a division belongs to an enterprise. The UI labels it for the
stage being created ("Division it belongs to" on a department, "Enterprise or
group" on a division), and hides it on enterprise, which has no parent.

VOUCHERS carry it too, plus a unit_label. Without the voucher half, the exact
path in the scenario above - issue vouchers for a department - would be the one
that loses the data. unit_label also fixes a second problem it exposed:
redemption derives scope_label from redeemer + company, producing "Sara Ali ·
Acme Bank", which is fine for a practice sitting and useless as a row in a
division comparison that needs to read "Compensation".

PAYOFF: the rollup panel now surfaces "2 assessments named this division when
they were set up" with a Link all button, matched case- and space-insensitively
because the names are typed by hand months apart.

Verified end-to-end against the real scenario: department created with a
division name, second department months later with the same one, a third in a
DIFFERENT division, then a division engagement - the panel suggests exactly the
first two and correctly excludes the third. Fixtures deleted after.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: fix the investment matrix - points were plotted outside the chart
entries.plain: Fixed the investment matrix chart where data points were plotting outside the visible area, so the chart now shows pillar positions correctly.
entries.explanation:
Client spotted it. Three defects, all real:

1. EVERY POINT WAS OUTSIDE THE PLOT BOX. Business value was normalised as
   pillar_weight / maxWeight, so with the default uniform weights (all 8 at
   12.5%) value resolved to 1.0 for every pillar, y landed exactly on the top
   edge, and the hash jitter then pushed the whole cohort above it - the dots
   floated over the "Quick Wins" label instead of sitting in a quadrant.

2. THE NORMALISATION WAS WRONG EVEN WHEN WEIGHTS VARY. Dividing by the maximum
   makes uniform weights read as MAXIMUM business value when they actually mean
   undifferentiated, and compresses genuinely different weights (10% and 15%)
   into the top of the axis. Now range-normalised across min..max, falling back
   to the midline when every pillar is weighted alike - which is the honest
   position for "this axis cannot separate them".

3. NOTHING CLAMPED THE JITTER, so a point could leave the axes regardless.
   Both coordinates are now clamped to keep the whole dot inside.

Also: hash jitter does not guarantee separation, and two pillars with close
scores (Governance 2.31, Model Management 2.42) overlapped with one number
unreadable. Added a deterministic de-overlap pass that pushes colliding pairs
apart along the line between them and re-clamps.

And the prose no longer contradicts the picture: "Focus on the top-left Quick
Wins quadrant first" pointed the reader at an empty quadrant whenever weights
are uniform. The intro now switches to reading the chart left to right, and the
matrix carries a note saying the vertical axis does not separate the pillars at
equal weights and where to set weights so it does.

Verified on the 40-respondent simulation: 8 points, 0 outside the plot box, no
overlaps, left-to-right order matches the gap ranking (Data 3.56 leftmost,
Governance 2.31 rightmost). 26 pages, none over the sheet.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: retire the Mode A/B/C shorthand for names that say what each mode is
entries.plain: Renamed the three personal deployment modes to clear names describing what each one is, replacing confusing Mode A/B/C labels.
entries.explanation:
"Mode C" meant nothing to anyone who had not read the code. The three personal
deployment modes are now named for what they are, everywhere:

  Mode A -> free personal snapshot
  Mode B -> paid personal deep-dive
  Mode C -> departmental plus personal

94 replacements across 29 files - comments, docs, CLAUDE.md, and the SQL
comments in two already-applied migrations (comment-only, no runtime effect;
changed so a reader of the schema history meets the same vocabulary).

Nothing user-facing changed: every occurrence was an implementation comment or
internal documentation. The letters had never appeared in a UI string, an email
or a report, which is worth recording because it means the rename carries no
client communication risk.

Replacement was ordered rather than a blind find-and-replace, so multi-word
phrasings were consumed before the bare tokens: "Mode B deep-dive" became "paid
personal deep-dive" rather than "paid personal deep-dive deep-dive", and
"Mode C is on" became "the departmental-plus-personal layer is on". The result
was then swept for doubled adjectives and article mismatches, which caught four
("Free free personal snapshot entry", "New paid paid personal deep-dive" and
two others) that the ordering alone did not prevent.

The CLAUDE.md modes table is re-keyed on the names and carries a note that the
letters were internal shorthand, so they do not creep back.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: mark the personal-results email retired by policy
entries.plain: Marked the personal results email as retired since employees never actually receive their individual scores under current policy.
entries.explanation:
The taker never sees their own results (XP-13): the personal results page
returns a thank-you card to anyone without a staff session, and the personal
PDF route 403s a token-only caller. The ara_personal_results_link template
tells the employee the opposite on all three counts - that the results page is
theirs to bookmark, that they can download the PDF, and that the page lists
their four factor scores.

It has no call site, so no employee has ever received it. Left as-is it is a
trap: wiring it up would silently reverse the confidentiality posture without
anyone noticing the page and PDF still refuse. Annotated with the reason, the
client confirmation (2026-09-01: the employee sees neither their factor scores
nor the report), and the order of operations if the policy is ever reversed -
change the gates first.

Copy kept rather than deleted so a reversal does not mean rewriting bilingual
content from scratch.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: cross-unit rollup - the Division / Enterprise deliverable
entries.plain: Built the ability to compare performance across multiple departments and divisions in a single rollup report.
entries.explanation:
A Division is composed of departments (HR = Learning & Development + Training
+ Compensation); an Enterprise is composed of divisions. Until now the only
cross-assessment link was prior_assessment_id, which is the SAME unit a year
later, so the one question a single-unit report can never answer - which units
are behind, and where they differ - was unreachable. With Department now
shipping the complete report, this comparison layer is what Division and
Enterprise actually sell.

MIGRATION 00200 (applied): ara_assessments.parent_assessment_id, a self-FK
with ON DELETE SET NULL so removing a rollup never destroys the unit
assessments under it, a partial index for the "children of X" read, and a
CHECK against self-parenting. Deliberately a self-FK rather than a groups
table: a rollup IS an assessment (org, region, stage, scope, its own report),
so one entity means one RLS policy and one ownership check.

LIBRARY src/lib/ara/unit-rollup.ts derives everything from the units'
already-computed pillar scores, so it can never disagree with the reports
underneath it. Each unit is averaged over ITS OWN pillar scope, so a pillar a
unit was never asked about cannot drag it down. The parent score is
respondent-weighted by default (a 40-person unit should not be outvoted by a
6-person one), with an equal-weight option.

The headline is variance, not the average: sharedGaps (every unit below 4.00 -
structural, fix once centrally) and unevenPillars (spread >= 1.00 - capability
that exists somewhere and has not travelled).

REPORT /ara/consultant/assessments/[id]/rollup + PDF at
/api/ara/reports/[id]/rollup/pdf - cover, cross-unit summary with gauge, units
ranked, a units x pillars matrix coloured by maturity level, and shared-versus-
uneven analysis. Not logged to ara_reports: a rollup is a view over children,
not a new report of the parent's own responses.

UI: "Units in this division" panel on the assessment overview - link, unlink,
open each unit, open the comparison. Shown on Division/Enterprise, and on any
engagement that already owns units so a link is never orphaned.

Guards: both sides of a link must be the caller's (otherwise a consultant
could pull another's assessment into their rollup and read its scores), same
organization only, no double-parenting, and a bounded ancestor walk rejects
longer cycles the DB CHECK cannot see. Unlink is scoped by parent so it can
only ever detach a unit genuinely under that rollup.

Verified end-to-end on a seeded HR division of three departments (26
respondents): division 3.21 In Progress, L&D 3.77 / Training 3.17 /
Compensation 2.57, 3 shared gaps, 4 uneven pillars, Operations 1.31 apart. 5
pages, no overflow. Rendering it surfaced a real omission I then fixed:
Strategy and Governance are in the division's scope but no department covered
them, which produced no row and no colour and read as "fine" - the report now
names them and says no evidence was collected, which is not the same as no gap.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: Department ships the complete report - tier is scope, not feature access
entries.plain: Department tier now includes the complete report with investment matrix and roadmap - these features are no longer reserved for higher tiers.
entries.explanation:
Commercial decision: most ARC demand is departmental, so the Department
deliverable IS the product and cannot be a stripped sample. The investment
priority matrix and the 12-month roadmap - the last two stage gates in the
report - are now ungated. The report contains NO stage gates at all.

What still varies is DATA (is there a prior assessment, are there use cases,
is the peer sample big enough) and SCOPE (how many pillars, how many
respondents). The one thing a Department engagement does not include is the
Phase 2 consultant validation workshop, which is consultant time rather than
report content and is already presented as a paid addition.

Also removed the appendix Disclaimer's gate: it was conditioned as a proxy for
"did the investment matrix render", which is no longer a question.

RE-MEASURED after the change (standard scope, Saudi / general, small cohort):
  Department  4 pillars = 21 pages (was 19)
  Division    6 pillars = 23
  Enterprise  8 pillars = 25
  Department  8 pillars, 40 respondents = 26 (the kept HR simulation)
Fixtures built, measured, then deleted; the HR simulation is untouched.

NOTE for whoever prices this: Department and Enterprise now produce nearly
identical documents at equal pillar scope - the remaining spread is pillar
count and roster length. If Enterprise is to be worth more it has to differ by
what is ASSESSED (multiple units compared, board-level respondents) rather
than by what the report is allowed to show, and no cross-unit rollup exists
yet - the only cross-assessment link today is year-on-year for the same unit.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: measure the real report length per tier, and fix the compliance overflow
entries.plain: Measured actual report page counts and fixed a formatting error that was causing content to overflow on the compliance pages.
entries.explanation:
Built one standard-scope run at each tier on the sandbox org, rendered each,
counted pages, then deleted the fixtures. Standard scope confirmed by the item
counts served: 49 / 71 / 99.

MEASURED (Saudi / general, cohort small enough that the roster fits the
profile page, so these are the floor the comparison table claims):
  Department  4 pillars,  4 respondents = 19 pages
  Division    6 pillars,  6 respondents = 23 pages
  Enterprise  8 pillars, 12 respondents = 25 pages
  Department  8 pillars, 40 respondents = 24 pages (the kept HR simulation)
The estimates in the previous commit (~19 / ~23 / ~25) were right, and are now
recorded as measurements rather than arithmetic.

BUG THE MEASUREMENT EXPOSED: the compliance section overflowed its sheet on
both the Department (310mm) and Division (305mm) runs. Two causes - the
first-page cap of 5 cards was set before the intro gained its basis note, and
Tier 1 turns out to hold up to 4 frameworks with the tier-boundary chunker
placing more on one page than fits. Caps lowered to 4 first page / 6 after,
and the oversize-tier split rewritten: the old loop recomputed its cap from
chunks.length WHILE pushing, so the slice width changed underneath it.

Also corrected the regulatory row, which the measurement showed I had made too
generous in the previous commit. It is not "All applicable" at every tier: a
framework is scored when its requirements touch a pillar in scope, so coverage
follows the pillar set - Department 5 frameworks, Division 6, Enterprise 7.
The row now says "Frameworks touching your N pillars", which is what the
engine actually does. "Top 3 frameworks" was still wrong.

Verified: no page in any of the four reports exceeds the sheet.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC: make the stage comparison table match what the report ships
entries.plain: Updated the public tier comparison table to accurately show what each tier actually receives, removing outdated marketing claims.
entries.explanation:
The public stage-comparison table (/ara/engage) had drifted into marketing
fiction. It sold Department as a stripped tier that in reality gets almost
everything, and it understated the deliverable badly. The whole report
contains exactly TWO stage gates - the investment matrix and the 12-month
roadmap, both `engagement_stage !== "department"`. Every other row was gated
by DATA (is there a prior assessment, are there use cases, is the peer sample
big enough), not by tier, so the table was promising less than we ship.

Corrected against the code that renders each feature:
- Shadow AI alert detection: claimed Division+. Not gated - Department gets it.
- Year-on-year reassessment: claimed Enterprise-only. The section is always
  rendered (it shows a baseline message until a comparable prior exists).
- AI use-case portfolio review: claimed Division+. Portfolio tab is available
  at every stage; the report section renders whenever use cases are logged.
- Layer 2 consultant guide questions: claimed Division+. The Phase 2 guide tab
  has no stage check.
- Regulatory framework mapping: claimed "Top 3 frameworks" for Department. No
  such limit exists in compliance.ts - every applicable framework is scored at
  every stage (the simulation scores all 7).
- Side-by-side bilingual report: claimed Enterprise-only. ?language=bilingual
  is accepted for any org assessment.
- Peer benchmarks: claimed Enterprise-only. Rendered on every org report; the
  column fills once 3+ comparable engagements exist. A data threshold, not a
  tier - now stated as such.
- Pillars assessed: "4 of 8 - you choose" ignored the custom-scope toggle,
  which allows any set of 1+ pillars with a per-pillar question budget.
- Report length: "8 / 27 / 27-60 pages" was far out. Length is 13 fixed pages
  plus one per in-scope pillar, plus compliance and roster pages, plus 2 for
  the strategic outputs - so a Department run with a custom 8-pillar scope and
  40 respondents renders 24, not 8. Replaced with "From ~19 / ~23 / ~25 pages"
  derived from that formula, and the same fix applied to
  ARA_STAGE_DEFINITIONS.report_pages, which feeds the wizard and /ara/engage.

Phase 2, Perception vs Reality, the investment matrix and the roadmap stay
Division+ - those four are genuinely enforced.

Added a header comment stating the rule: before setting any cell to false,
point at the code that enforces it; if nothing does, the cell is true and the
tiering has to be built first.

Verified by rendering /ara/engage.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: cross-reference Phase 2 by page, and fix the last two claim sites
entries.plain: Fixed page references to Phase 2 so they point to the correct location in the report where Phase 2 is explained.
entries.explanation:
Two more places asserted the Phase 2 workshop as something already coming to
the client: the per-pillar "Key findings" empty state ("Detailed findings will
be added by the consultant during the Phase 2 workshop") and the band-chart
caption ("worth probing in the Phase 2 workshop"). Both render on every pillar
page, and on a Department engagement neither is true. They now read from the
engagement stage and, where Phase 2 is optional, point the reader at the panel
that explains it.

NEW PageRef component resolves those pointers to a real page number ("see Next
Steps, page 18"). The page a section lands on shifts with stage, pillar count,
framework count and roster size, so it measures DOM order rather than trusting
a number written at authoring time.

It is a CLIENT component on purpose. The first cut stamped the text with an
inline script, which worked and was then silently REVERTED by hydration -
React re-rendered the server markup over it and logged a text-content mismatch
("Server: Next Steps, page 18 / Client: Next Steps"). Rendering the label on
the server and appending the number in an effect keeps both renders identical
at hydration, so the number sticks. The bare label remains a correct fallback:
if the effect never runs the reference still reads "see Next Steps".

Verified: all 9 references resolve to page 18 (the actual Next Steps page) and
are present in the DOM at the moment page.pdf() captures, no hydration
warnings, 24 pages, none over the sheet.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: explain Phase 2, and stop promising it to tiers that lack it
entries.plain: Clarified what Phase 2 workshops are in the report and stopped promising them to department engagements that do not include them.
entries.explanation:
The report leaned on "the Phase 2 workshop" as the thing that would verify
its findings, in three places, without ever telling the reader what Phase 2
is - and Phase 2 is a Division/Enterprise deliverable (ARA_STAGE_MAP marks it
department: false, and this report already gates the investment matrix and
roadmap on the same line). A Department client was being promised a
validation step their engagement does not include.

Rather than delete the references, the report now sells it properly:

- NEW Phase 2 panel on Next Steps, labelled "(included in this engagement)"
  or "(optional addition)" from the engagement stage. It explains, in the
  client's terms, that every score above is self-reported and Phase 2 is the
  facilitated session that tests those answers against evidence: the
  pillar-by-pillar evidence review using the consultant probing questions
  respondents never see, the perception-versus-reality gap, the validated
  maturity band recorded alongside the self-assessed one, and the written
  findings plus gap-ranked capability plan issued as an updated report. A
  Department reader is told plainly it is not included and to ask for a quote.
- The appendix "honest limits" row, the compliance basis line, and the
  Shadow AI callout now describe Phase 2 as an optional addition when the
  stage does not include it, instead of stating it as a given.

Also: the appendix Disclaimer defined what "investment signals" mean, but the
investment matrix and roadmap are gated out of Department reports - so it
explained a chart that reader never saw. Gated on the same condition.

Verified on the Stage 1 simulation: 24 pages, none over the sheet, the panel
reads "(optional addition)" and the orphaned disclaimer is gone.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: running footer - issuer left, page number right
entries.plain: Added running footer to every report page showing the organization name on the left and page number on the right.
entries.explanation:
Every page except the cover now carries a footer: "Virginia Institute of
Finance and Management" on the left, the page number on the right.

Built with CSS counters rather than Puppeteer's footerTemplate because the
PDF route renders with preferCSSPageSize and `@page { margin: 0 }`, and a
Puppeteer header/footer draws inside the page margin - with no margin it
would be clipped away entirely. One .report-page is exactly one sheet, so
incrementing the counter per section yields a true page number.

The cover suppresses the footer (grey text on the navy full-bleed page would
be unreadable, and it already signs itself off in its own footer row) but
still increments, so the page after the cover is numbered 2.

Verified under print emulation: page box 296mm, footer at 10mm from the
bottom edge inside the existing 20mm padding, so it displaces no content;
PDF still renders 24 pages with no page over the sheet.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: critical read of the back half - real fixes, no invented claims
entries.plain: ARC reports now correctly state how long your assessment data is kept - matching the actual 2-year retention policy, not a false promise of 3 years.
entries.explanation:
Second pass of the page-by-page read, covering compliance through appendix,
plus two defects the client caught on the executive page.

CLAIMS THAT WERE NOT TRUE
- RETENTION: the notice promised the client "three years" while the purge job
  deletes at ARA_RETENTION_YEARS = 2. It both contradicted the maximum-2-year
  commitment we sell on and promised access to data that would already be
  gone. Now derived from the constant, and it says accurately what survives
  (reports are detached and kept as business records; the assessment record
  and supporting materials are purged).
- SHADOW AI: the alert told the client "employees may be using public AI tools
  without formal organizational approval ... immediate action required" even
  when nothing in the responses said so. The detector fires on EITHER a
  keyword match in open text OR any governance item scored <= 2.0, and only
  the first is evidence of tool use. The copy now follows the signal: named
  tools are reported with the count; the governance-only case is stated as
  what it is, a control gap that leaves unsanctioned use undetectable, "not a
  finding of misuse".
- COMPLIANCE: a page of framework names and percentages read as a legal audit
  with no statement of basis. Added one, and relabelled the figure from
  "Compliant" (it sat above "0 Met" on every framework) to "Requirements
  covered", which is what the weighted met+half-partial number measures.

CONSISTENCY WITH ARC'S OWN VOCABULARY
- The appendix fact sheet taught a SECOND, contradictory maturity ladder -
  "initial, developing, defined, managed, optimised" - for the same number
  page 1 reports on ARA_MATURITY_LEVELS (L1 Unaware ... L5 Leading). It is now
  generated from that constant, EN and AR, and states that 4.00 is the target
  rather than the top of the scale. The Arabic fact sheet also still carried
  the "calibrated against UAE and Saudi frameworks" overclaim; corrected to
  match the English.

THINGS THE READER COULD NOT FIND OR READ
- EXEC PANELS (client-reported): the narrative counted "4 approaching, 4
  requiring focus" while the panels showed 3 and 3, so two pillars appeared
  nowhere. Both panels now list their whole category and carry the count, so
  they sum to the in-scope pillars.
- GAUGE (client-reported): the band label baseline sits below the viewBox
  height I had set, slicing "Early Stage" in half. Height is now derived from
  that baseline.
- PILLAR PROFILE CHART: the 30-character label cap clipped exactly the two
  longest pillar names to "...Portfol..." and "...Complian...", on a chart
  whose only job is naming pillars.
- COMPLIANCE TIERS: pagination sliced by count, so Tier 2 split across pages
  and each page announced "TIER 2 - 1 FRAMEWORK" for a tier holding two. Now
  chunked on tier boundaries with the true per-tier total.
- NEXT STEPS promised services "mapped to the gaps identified in this
  assessment" and then printed the same five for everyone. They are now
  ordered by this cohort's gaps and name the pillar and score each addresses.
- ROSTER: three pages of a four-column table where two columns were "-" for
  every respondent. Empty columns are dropped, and a Name+Status roster
  renders two-up. Forty respondents now take two pages, not three.
- Raw enum "active" and internal shorthand "Not yet" no longer leak into the
  client-facing methodology table.

Verified on the 40-respondent simulation: 24 pages, no page exceeds the
sheet, no truncated labels, panels reconcile 4 + 4 = 8.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: critical-read pass - percentages, real defects, no em dashes
entries.plain: ARC reports now accurately show whether your organization is ahead of or behind AI-readiness targets, fixing a critical misreading that made scores appear better than they were.
entries.explanation:
Read the rendered report page by page rather than patching reported
symptoms. Fixes, all verified on the 40-respondent simulation:
- PROGRESS AS % OF TARGET (client request): "+1.69 vs benchmark" read as
  being AHEAD of target when it meant 1.69 BELOW it. Every surface now
  states progress as a share of the 4.00 AI Ready target - critical gaps
  ("2.31 - 58% of target"), the pillar metric strip ("Progress to target
  67%"), and the benchmark comparison column.
- RADAR LABELS: label.split(" & ") silently DROPPED the ampersand, so
  pillars rendered as "Strategy / Vision". The wrap now keeps it.
- KPI TILES: the strip repeated the maturity band (already in the tile
  beside it and in the gauge) and did not reconcile - "0 at/above" plus
  "4 requiring focus" left 4 pillars unaccounted for. Replaced with
  At/above target + Approaching target + Requiring focus, which sums to
  the in-scope count; the narrative follows suit.
- DEAD STRENGTHS PANEL: with nothing at 4.0 the panel just said "none
  yet". It now shows RELATIVE strengths (highest-scoring pillars with
  their % of target) so the reader still learns where the ground is best.
- PROVISIONAL BANNER: moved ONTO the cover. As a sibling above the page
  sections it joined the print flow, offsetting every page (the cover's
  footer bled onto page 2); as its own page it wasted a sheet.
- GAUGE: score, "/ 5.0" and the band label now stack clear of the needle
  sweep, with the canvas extended so nothing is clipped.
- PER-PILLAR RECOMMENDATIONS: the generator keyed only on the score band
  and interpolated the pillar name, so every pillar in a band repeated
  the same three actions and the same expected outcomes. Replaced with a
  library of pillar-specific actions across the four maturity bands.
- "CALIBRATED AGAINST <region> FRAMEWORKS" overclaimed a calibration that
  does not happen; the score is a weighted average and compliance is
  assessed separately against the applicable frameworks (EN + AR).
- EM/EN DASHES removed per project convention: 314 across 72 source
  files, plus the database copy they came from (6 regulatory framework
  names, 90 questions' citation blocks). Rendered report now contains 0.
Report: 25 pages, no section exceeding a sheet.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: meaningful heatmap, explicit 1-5 scale, self-healing compliance
entries.plain: ARC reports now display a meaningful readiness heatmap showing how many people are at each skill level, replacing a confusing internal-numbering grid.
entries.explanation:
Client review:
- GAP HEATMAP: the "Q1-2 / Q3-4 / Q5-6 / Q7-8 / Q9+" columns were the
  question bank's INTERNAL item numbers grouped in pairs - an arbitrary
  split with no meaning to a reader, and one that rendered ragged empty
  cells whenever a custom-scope run served non-contiguous item numbers.
  Replaced with a cohort maturity DISTRIBUTION: pillars x the canonical
  L1-L5 levels, each cell counting respondents, shaded by concentration.
  Axis derives from ARA_MATURITY_LEVELS so it cannot drift.
- SCALE CLARITY: readers twice read 4.0 as the ceiling. The heatmap page
  now states plainly that scores run 1.00-5.00 and 4.00 is the AI Ready
  target, not the maximum, with L4/L5 sitting above it.
- COMPLIANCE SHOWING ZEROS: the compliance engine is triggered manually
  from the consultant console, so an assessment with scored responses but
  no compliance run rendered every framework as "N requirements, 0 met,
  0 partial, 0 action" - which reads as total non-compliance. summarize
  now self-heals (computes when results are absent but responses exist),
  and the card renders an explicit "not yet evaluated" line (EN + AR)
  instead of zeros whenever a framework genuinely has no results.
Verified on the 40-respondent simulation: heatmap shows the L1-L5
distribution, and Saudi PDPL now reports 0 met / 5 partial / 3 action.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: kill print bleed, drop invented peer figure, reorder, fix gauge
entries.plain: ARC reports no longer print with content bleeding onto extra pages, and fake benchmark figures have been removed.
entries.explanation:
Client review round:
- PAGE BLEED (root cause): .report-page carries a 10mm bottom margin +
  shadow for the on-screen preview, making each print box 307mm inside a
  297mm sheet - a sliver of every page bled onto the next. Print media now
  zeroes the margin/shadow and holds min-height just under A4. Verified:
  every section measures under the sheet height.
- INVENTED BENCHMARK: the peer column showed a hardcoded "GCC Best 4.50"
  when no peer data existed - an unsourced figure above the 4.00 AI Ready
  target (4.5 is merely the L5 threshold). It now renders "-" under a
  "Peer median (pending)" header, and the copy states medians unlock at N
  comparable engagements with 4.00 remaining the reference target.
- Organization Profile (+ its roster continuation pages) moved to the end
  of the report, before the Appendix.
- Maturity gauge: the score label sat in the needle's sweep and was
  struck through at mid-range scores; moved below the hub.
- Removed the "How to sequence" boilerplate repeated on all 8 pillar pages.
Simulation PDF: 26 clean pages.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: eliminate page bleed - every section ends on its own page
entries.plain: ARC reports now fit properly on printed pages - employee rosters and compliance sections are split intelligently across multiple pages instead of spilling over.
entries.explanation:
Client feedback: several pages carried tail content bleeding from the
previous section. Root causes + fixes:
- Organization Profile carried the full respondent roster (40 rows =
  +826px): roster now paginates - 16 rows on the profile page, the rest
  distributed EVENLY across clean "(continued)" pages (no orphan pages).
- Regulatory Compliance (+475px): frameworks paginate 5-first-page /
  7-per-continuation with proper headers; Shadow-AI callout rides the
  last page.
- Appendix (+1727px): split into clean pages - fact sheet + methodology,
  anchor instruments (paginated 14/18 per page), then validity +
  weights + disclaimers; scoring copy aligned with the renormalised
  weighting.
- Pillar Overview (+21px): radar 440->416 + tighter profile chart rows.
- Pillar deep-dives (+2px rounding): margins shaved.
Verified in print emulation: ZERO sections exceed one page height; the
40-respondent simulation PDF renders 27 clean pages.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: one page per pillar deep-dive
entries.plain: ARC reports now fit one pillar deep-dive per page, reducing report length and making it easier to review printed findings.
entries.explanation:
Findings + Recommendations merged onto a single A4 page per pillar
(client request): shared header, metric strip, respondent-spread band
chart, key findings, then a two-column recommendation grid (odd last
card spans full width) with the sequencing guidance as a compact line.
Card paddings and section margins tightened; verified under print
emulation that all eight pillar sections fit exactly one page (zero
overflow) on the 40-respondent simulation. Cuts eight pages from the
departmental PDF.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC consistency audit: one canonical vocabulary across every surface
entries.plain: ARC now uses consistent language everywhere - dashboard, reports, and all languages - so terms like readiness levels mean the same thing in every place you see them.
entries.explanation:
Five-auditor sweep of ARC (dashboard, portrait report, bilingual report,
personal/workforce surfaces, codebase-wide) against the canonical
standards. Dashboard: fully canonical. Fixes shipped:
- Exec KPI tile said "Below benchmark" while counting < 3.0 -> relabelled
  "Requiring focus / Pillars scoring < 3.00" (truthful; benchmark is 4.0).
- Heatmap legends (portrait inline + i18n EN/AR) used invented vocabulary
  ("Critical", "Early stage") -> canonical pillar labels Unaware /
  Exploring / Developing / Advancing+ with exact ranges.
- "Advanced" (overall-band word) fixed to "Advancing" (pillar word) in
  FindingsPanel + report-i18n EN/AR; AR "below Developing" wording fixed.
- Hardcoded "eight pillars" copy (exec/how-to-read/workforce, EN+AR) ->
  scope-neutral wording, correct on 4/6/custom runs; appendix scoring
  copy updated to the implemented renormalised weighting.
- Maturity gauge arcs now ITERATE ARA_OVERALL_BANDS + use
  overallBandFromScore (no duplicated thresholds/colours).
- Personal factor tone trio (Strong/Developing/Opportunity) centralised
  as ARA_FACTOR_TONES + getFactorTone; four hand-typed copies replaced;
  Arabic mode now shows Arabic tone labels; AR PDF middle-band word
  unified to the results page's canonical term.
- Voucher insights: stage labels from ARA_INDIVIDUAL_MATURITY_STAGES,
  norm-unlock copy interpolates MIN_NORM_SAMPLE.
- Bilingual AR maturity label reads stored maturity_label_ar (helper
  string-match kept only as fallback).
Verified against the 40-respondent HR simulation.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: align every maturity label with the canonical L1-L5 model
entries.plain: ARC now aligns all maturity labels with a standard five-level model so readiness descriptions stay consistent and accurate across the entire report.
entries.explanation:
Client review caught the band chart using invented zone labels instead of
the canonical five-level model. Zones now derive directly from
ARA_MATURITY_LEVELS (L1 Unaware / L2 Exploring / L3 Developing /
L4 Advancing / L5 Leading, boundaries 2.0/3.0/4.0/4.5) so they can never
drift again. Also fixed a PRE-EXISTING mismatch the review surfaced: the
deep-dive maturity tiles derived their L-number by ceiling the raw score
(2.66 showed "Exploring L3" while the engine says L2) - portrait and
bilingual variants now quote the engine's maturity_level.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: ranked profile chart + respondent-spread band charts
entries.plain: ARC reports now include two new charts - a ranked readiness bar chart and a scatter view showing where each person falls within readiness bands.
entries.explanation:
Two visualization upgrades to the portrait report (print-safe inline SVG,
brand palette):
- Radar page gains a "Ranked readiness profile": every in-scope pillar as
  a sorted horizontal bar on the 1-5 scale, maturity-coloured, with a
  dashed AI-Ready 4.0 reference line and value labels.
- Each pillar deep-dive replaces the plain benchmark progress bar with a
  maturity BAND chart: the five zones (Nascent -> Leading), one dot per
  respondent's pillar mean (stacked deterministically, so cohort
  agreement/disagreement is visible at a glance), the cohort mean marker,
  and the dashed benchmark - plus an explanatory caption. Powered by a
  new per-respondent pillar-mean computation over the already-paginated
  response rows (org Layer-1 items only).
Verified on the simulated 40-respondent HR department run.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: replace accent-edge cards with editorial VIFM styling
entries.plain: ARC report card styling now matches VIFM branding, removing generic-looking colored borders in favor of professional navy and key indicators.
entries.explanation:
The 3pt colored top borders on rounded cards + bright rounded pill pairs
(teal QUICK WIN / amber MEDIUM EFFORT) read as generic AI-generated
design. Restyled the three card families in report-primitives:
- RecommendationCard: navy number block, title, and a quiet uppercase
  meta line (small square key in the horizon colour + "Quick Win | Medium
  effort" as text) - no pills, no coloured edge; solid hairline above the
  outcome row.
- StatTile: coloured top edge replaced by a small square key before the
  uppercase label.
- FindingsPanel: coloured top edge dropped (the icon + title already
  carry the semantic colour).
Verified on the simulated 40-respondent HR report.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC portrait report: reduced-form caveat + workforce note (EN/AR)
entries.plain: ARC portrait reports now include important notes about scope and workforce evidence, matching the bilingual report's completeness.
entries.explanation:
The custom-scope caveat and the Talent/Culture person-level-evidence note
shipped only in the bilingual layout; the default EN and AR portrait flows
render inline in the report page and were missing both. Ported: the exec
summary carries the reduced-form caveat (with the real pillar count +
question budget), and PillarPages gains a workforceNote strip passed for
Talent/Culture when the individual layer has answered data. Verified on a
simulated 40-respondent HR department run (8 pillars x 6 questions).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC respondent form: option shapes, sequential numbering, no hint link
entries.plain: ARC respondent form now displays all answer options correctly and numbers questions sequentially, fixing missing radio buttons and confusing jumps.
entries.explanation:
Three client-reported fixes on the respondent form:
- Blank option rows: the renderer assumed {value,label} option objects,
  but most bank questions store plain string arrays (185 vs 12), so every
  string-shaped MCQ/yes-no rendered empty radio rows. Options are now
  normalized to both shapes (string text = the stored answer value, which
  score_map keys on) - mirrors the admin editor's normalization.
- Question numbers jumped (Q4, Q7, Q17...) because cards fell back to
  bank question_number; subset forms (custom scope) made it worse. Display
  numbering is now sequential Q1..Qn across the whole served form in
  section render order (pillars -> factors -> agentic).
- "Show hint" removed from the respondent form (help_text stays in the
  bank for the consultant guide).
Verified in the preview on a custom 48-question sitting: options render,
numbering runs Q1..Q48, no hint affordance.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC report: workforce-evidence note under Talent + Culture deep-dives
entries.plain: ARC Talent and Culture deep-dives now point to individual workforce data when available, connecting personal factors to organizational impact.
entries.explanation:
When a Mode C engagement measured the individual layer (workforce rollup
has data), the Talent and Culture pillar deep-dives carry a bilingual
"person-level evidence" note pointing at the Workforce AI Readiness
section - the designed bridge between the 4 personal factors and the two
pillars where individual capability lives institutionally. Renders only
when the individual layer is on and answered.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC voucher wizard: full stage ladder with standard-design presets
entries.plain: ARC voucher creation now offers all four assessment levels - Personal, Department, Division, and Enterprise - each with preset question counts you can customize.
entries.explanation:
The Assessment selector now offers all four levels - Personal ARC
(individual), Department (Stage 1), Division (Stage 2), Enterprise
(Stage 3). Picking a stage presets the STANDARD design (the stage's
default pillars + the full question set: 49 / 71 / 99 questions), which
the admin can then customize (swap pillars, set a per-pillar budget).
Enterprise locks the pillar picker to all 8 (the runtime always serves
all 8 there); the footnote and design chip follow the chosen stage.
Verified: a Division standard voucher redemption serves exactly 71
questions across its 6 default pillars.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC voucher wizard: align questions-per-pillar on the options row
entries.plain: ARC voucher form layout is now cleaner - the questions-per-pillar field sits flush with other controls instead of floating above the row.
entries.explanation:
The inline hint under the input made its block taller than Assessment /
Region, floating the field above the row baseline. Field is now
label+input only (guidance moved to the input tooltip + the panel
footnote), so Assessment, Questions per pillar and Region sit flush on
one line.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC org-design panel: align with the bank + region; pre-cap region fix
entries.plain: AI Readiness assessment numbers now match what clients will actually receive, including correct regional availability and a warning if any skill area falls short.
entries.explanation:
The voucher org-design panel now aligns its numbers with what a redemption
will actually serve: per-pillar availability is computed from the ACTIVE
bank with region isolation applied (voucher runs are sector-general), the
pillar cards show "6 of 8"-style served-vs-available counts for the
effective region (tagged client's region, else the form region), the
header chip shows the TRUE total that will be served, and a warning names
any pillar whose bank falls short of the budget.

Correctness fix underneath: the region/sector filter ran AFTER
capPerPillar/capPerFactor, so a region-specific item inside the capped
window would silently shrink a pillar below its designed budget. Both
serve paths now filter to region/sector-eligible items BEFORE capping,
and both write-path kept-set reconstructions mirror the same order.
Verified: Saudi-region voucher e2e serves exactly 48 (6 x 8).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC voucher wizard: free numeric questions-per-pillar input
entries.plain: Admins can now set any custom number of questions per skill area (1-20) instead of choosing from preset options.
entries.explanation:
Replace the preset dropdown (4/5/6/8/full) with a free number input
(1-20, blank = full set) so the admin picks any question budget, matching
the assessment wizard's control. Pillar count stays freely selectable 1-8
via the picker.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC vouchers: carry the org assessment design (pillars + questions)
entries.plain: Redemption codes can now deliver customized multi-skill assessments, letting clients test their full AI readiness design before rolling out to employees.
entries.explanation:
A voucher can now provision the CUSTOMIZED org pillar assessment, not just
the personal 4-factor ARC - so a client can self-serve a designed test
drive (e.g. all 8 pillars at 6 questions each = 48 items) from a redeem
code. Migration 00199 (applied) adds engagement_stage / pillars_in_scope /
questions_per_pillar to ara_vouchers.

- Voucher wizard: "Assessment" select (Personal ARC | Org pillar
  assessment) with a pillar picker + questions-per-pillar budget; wired
  into both the code-batch and email-delegates paths.
- Redemption provisions a department-stage assessment carrying the
  voucher's designed scope (custom-scope levers 00029/00198); personal
  vouchers are byte-for-byte unchanged, tolerant of a pre-00199 DB.
Verified end-to-end: create org voucher -> public redeem -> respondent
served exactly 48 questions (6 per pillar across all 8).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: ARC custom scope: any pillar set + questions-per-pillar budget
entries.plain: Admins can now pick any combination of skill areas and set a custom question budget per area, giving complete flexibility in assessment design.
entries.explanation:
Alongside the untouched standard tiers (department=4 / division=6 /
enterprise=8 pillars, full question sets), the new-assessment wizard gains
a "Custom scope (advanced)" toggle: pick ANY pillar combination and set a
per-pillar question budget (e.g. an HR department run covering all 8
pillars at 6 questions each = 48 items). Migration 00198 adds
ara_assessments.questions_per_pillar (applied).

- Serve path caps each pillar deterministically (objective items first,
  curated order) via capPerPillar; the write path mirrors the cap so
  capped-out items can't be answered (same discipline as items_per_factor).
- Reassessment carries the custom scope forward; detail page shows a
  "Custom scope" badge; the bilingual report carries a reduced-form caveat
  (indicative, not benchmark-comparable to full forms).
Verified end-to-end: wizard -> DB (8 pillars, qpp=6) -> respondent form
serving exactly 48 questions (6 per pillar).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Enhance ARC detailed report + disable caching on sample pages
entries.plain: AI Readiness reports now include executive summaries, 30/60/90-day development plans, and manager guides; shared demo links update instantly.
