tsc + lint clean.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Role Readiness engine: migration + scoring + data libs (foundation)
entries.plain: Role Readiness assessments now have a complete foundation with database tables for roles, competencies, technical items, and candidate results.
entries.explanation:
The role-configurable Persona+Techno "role readiness" engine that surfaces inside
the existing Bespoke Services section. This is the verified foundation:

- migration 00153 (applied + verified live, 8 tables + 5 enums): job_families,
  rr_role_configs, rr_technical_areas, rr_technical_items, rr_competency_suggestions,
  rr_candidates, rr_section_results, bespoke_services. Additive; mirrors the
  Pre-Hire RLS pattern; technical items isolated from tech_assessment_items so
  sample/seed data can't leak into the real Techno bank.
- src/lib/role-readiness/scoring.ts (pure): per-side score vs threshold (inclusive
  >=), overall READY iff both pass, edge cases (no items, divide-by-zero, exact
  threshold, missing answers). scripts/test-role-readiness-scoring.ts proves
  CONDITION 4 (pass one side / fail other => not_ready) + 5 more cases: ALL PASS.
- src/lib/role-readiness/{config,candidate-access}.ts + src/lib/bespoke/services.ts:
  load a role config (competencies+targets reused from role_profiles, technical
  areas/items), token candidate lookup, and persist/load bespoke_services.

Next: admin role editor, combined candidate sitting + report, landing surfacing,
HR GM seed, full 8-condition verification.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Bespoke Services: landing entry + admin composer (front-end)
entries.plain: Bespoke Services is now a distinct offering on the platform - VIFM can bundle any combination of assessments and assign them to specific clients.
entries.explanation:
Adds a "Bespoke Services" meta-service: VIFM combines any of the platform's
services into one tailored package and assigns it to a client.

- Landing page: a distinct bespoke band below the service grid (bilingual EN/AR,
  RTL-aware), teasing the bundle-able services, linking to the composer. Hidden
  in client-portal mode (VIFM designs these). Opens /admin/bespoke.
- /admin/bespoke: admin-gated page (requireRole + notFound on the IDOR rail)
  that loads the real platform client list and renders the composer.
- BespokeBuilder: name (EN/AR) + description, multi-select of the 7 client
  services (icon/accent toggle cards), assign-to-client picker, a live preview
  card and a session list of composed packages.

This is the front-end pass. Persisting a bespoke service and surfacing it in the
assigned client's portal is the next step (to wire alongside the first design).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Portal: UUID-validate admin-preview orgParam (fail-fast)
entries.plain: Admin preview links are now validated more carefully to prevent unclear errors when accessing the system.
entries.explanation:
Low-severity hardening from the pool-voucher review: the admin-only preview
path passed orgParam straight through; validate its UUID shape in
resolveActorOrg so a malformed id fails with a clear message instead of an
opaque RPC error. Not a security boundary (admin-gated; RPC type-coerces).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Vouchers: individual + shared-link (seat-pool) modes everywhere
entries.plain: Vouchers now support both individual codes and shared links everywhere - managers can send one link to multiple people instead of emailing codes to each person.
entries.explanation:
Client portal previously only emailed individual single-use codes; the
admin Techno page hid its seat-pool behind a defaulted dropdown. Now every
voucher surface offers BOTH modes:

- Client portal (Fluent/Logica/Persona/Techno generic panel): new
  'Individual codes' | 'One shared link' toggle. Pool mode draws N seats
  from the allocation up-front and mints ONE code with max_uses=N via the
  service engine (no per-recipient email - the manager shares one link).
  New issueClientPoolVoucher() lib fn + clientIssuePoolVoucherAction;
  release-on-failure + Persona scope / Techno function threaded through
  exactly like the individual path. Engines unchanged (all already support
  maxUses / maxUsesPerCode).
- Admin Techno: dropdown -> visible two-button toggle (Individual codes |
  One shared link - many seats).
- Admin Fluent/Logica/Persona already expose both via How-many + Seats/code.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Client portal: render the exact platform landing in client mode
entries.plain: The client portal home page now displays the same professional layout as the main platform, showing available services with usage stats and expiry dates.

Replace the bespoke portal Home with the real PlatformLanding component in an

two-column Talent Acquisition / Talent Development families + rich service

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Client portal: redesign Home to match the admin platform landing
entries.plain: The client portal home has been redesigned with a branded header and service tiles that match the admin platform look, making it easier to see what's available.

The portal Home was a plain stacked-card list. Rebuild it with the same
polished look as the admin landing: a branded gradient hero (org name +
seats summary) and per-service jewel tiles (launcher-card tone-<hue>, same
icon + hue per service as the admin landing). Allocated services are active

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Client portal Phase 2: seat services (ARC, Reflect, Pre-Hire)

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Replace pre-existing em dashes with hyphens (SOP)
entries.plain: Text formatting has been standardized for consistency across the platform.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Add admin Competency Framework reference page
entries.plain: Admins can now view the complete behavioural framework in one place, showing all domains, competency groups, and skill definitions.
entries.explanation:
New /admin/framework page renders the full VIFM behavioural framework on
one screen: 4 domains, 9 clusters (each with a definition) and 41
competencies (each with its description). Sourced live from
competency_domains / _clusters / competencies; domain + cluster
definitions authored in framework-definitions.ts (the DB stores no
description for domains/clusters). Linked from the Platform sidebar group
as "Competency Framework" (Network icon), EN + AR nav labels.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: BPS phase 3: centre roles and competence records (B6)
entries.plain: Assessment centres can now record and display who manages the centre and what qualifications they hold, answering client questions about centre leadership.
entries.explanation:
Migration 00213 (applied). Fifteen clauses, and the direct answer to the
question that started this workstream: who ran this centre, and what
makes them qualified to have run it.

The platform knew about assessors and nobody else. A centre had no
manager, no administrator, no record that anyone was competent at
anything, and nothing to show a client who asked.

Three pieces. The role catalogue (src/lib/ac/centre-roles.ts) holds the
ten roles the standard names, each with what that person must be able
to do - in code, like the technical framework, because the standard
fixes it. ac_role_competence records who has DEMONSTRATED competence
for a role: the evidence field is required for a confirmation, because
5.22 asks us to confirm competence was demonstrated and 'we sent them
on a course' is not that, and expires_on lets competence lapse rather
than stand forever. ac_engagement_roles records who held which role at
which centre, including the client's own people, for whom 3.12 still
makes us responsible.

Requirements are read from the design, not asked: a role-play needs a
role-player, a combined or technical engagement needs a Psychometric
Test User (5.17), and a development centre needs feedback roles while a
selection centre does not (4.43), because its outcome is the arithmetic
rule. Every centre needs a Manager and an Administrator (5.16).

Activation is gated on it, beside the existing assessor staffing gate:
unfilled required roles and anyone assigned without current competence
both block (5.22, 6.2), overridable only with a recorded reason. One
person holding three roles is a caution, not a block.

13 unit tests. Verified on the live database: constraints and the CHECK
hold, and the staff-visibility policy does not recurse - my first draft
had it SELECT its own table from inside its own policy, which Postgres
refuses outright.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: BPS phase 2, batch 2b: a report goes nowhere the participant did not agree
entries.plain: Assessment reports can no longer be sent to anyone the participant has not agreed to, protecting participant privacy.
entries.explanation:
Migration 00212 (applied). Closes B26, and with it phase 2.

The joining pack names who receives reports and the participant agrees
to that list before attending (5.13, shipped in 00211). This is what
happens when anyone else asks: ac_report_disclosures turns it into a
question the participant answers, and the answer is kept either way. A
refusal is the more valuable record - it evidences that the question
was asked at all.

The database enforces what the workflow promises, verified against the
live database: the request itself cannot be edited after it is made, a
refusal cannot be overwritten with a grant, a decided request cannot be
walked back to pending, and a report recorded as handed over cannot be
un-handed-over. Withdrawing a permission already given IS allowed,
because a participant may change their mind and the standard does not
say otherwise. markDisclosureReleasedAction refuses to record a share
without a grant behind it.

Surfaces: the participant decides on their own welcome page, where the
request shows who asked, their role and why, with the wording that
saying no does not affect their results or how they are treated. Admins
ask from the engagement panel, which also states the agreed recipients
so the boundary being crossed is visible at the moment of crossing it.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: BPS phase 2, batch 2a: the joining pack and reasonable adjustments
entries.plain: Participants now receive a customized information pack before attending, explaining the centre's purpose, schedule, what happens, and who sees results.
entries.explanation:
Migration 00211 (applied).

B7, the joining pack (5.38-5.41, 3.17, 5.11, 5.12, 5.13, 5.8). Consent
was a page of generic text with no centre in it: a participant agreed
before being told what the centre was for, what would happen, who would
see the result or how long it is kept. Consent given without that is
not informed consent, which is what the whole of section 5 turns on.

The pack is GENERATED from the design - purpose, dates, exercises and
their timings, including a line saying when they are and are not being
assessed (6.5) - and the engagement stores only what the design cannot
know. A pack typed by hand drifts from the centre it describes, and a
participant told the wrong thing consented to the wrong thing. The same
builder feeds the admin checklist, so the checklist and the pack cannot
disagree about what is missing, and publishing is refused while any
clause item is unanswered.

Consent now carries the centre's own facts: agreeing the named report
recipients is required (5.13), research use is a separate optional
consent (5.8), retention is stated (5.41.6), and the form waits if the
pack has not been read. The consent page became a server wrapper around
the existing client form, which its own TODO had asked for.

B8, reasonable adjustments (5.45-5.47, 4.10). Every participant is
asked, so not_asked and none_needed are different states - someone
never asked cannot be said to have declined. Admins agree or refuse
with a reason, and what was agreed reaches the assessor on the
observation screen with the instruction not to treat it as evidence.
An adjustment agreed and not delivered is worse than one refused.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: One date for a record, and honest button names
entries.plain: Appeal dates now display consistently across all screens, and button labels now accurately describe what will happen when you click them.
entries.explanation:
Live end-to-end test of the appeals route surfaced two defects.

The same appeal read 21 September on the participant's page and 22
September on the admin panel. The participant page is a server
component, so it formatted in the server's UTC; the panel is a client
component and formatted in the reader's timezone. Every Caliber user is
UTC+3 or UTC+4, so anything raised after 20:00 local crossed the
boundary - on a record whose whole value is being trusted later. New
LocalDate component (and a formatLocalDate for client code) renders
every timestamp in the reader's timezone on both sides, matching the
server on first paint so nothing rehydrates badly. Date-only columns are
printed as stored, with no timezone shift at all.

The kind and stage buttons carried a title attribute, which becomes the
accessible name: a screen reader announced "An appeal" as "You believe
a result is wrong", so the visible label was not in the name. Hint text
was already on screen under the buttons, so the title is gone and
aria-pressed now says which one is chosen.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: BPS phase 2, batch 1: a participant can raise something and be told
entries.plain: Participants can now raise concerns or appeals directly from their portal, admins can respond in writing, and both sides see the full conversation thread.
entries.explanation:
Three duties with nowhere to live before. Migration 00210 (applied).

Concerns and appeals (5.44, 5.48, 6.11). ac_participant_concerns: the
participant raises it from their own portal before, during or after the
centre; admins answer it in writing; both sides see the thread. A
response cannot be rewritten once given and what was raised cannot be
edited, enforced by trigger, because an appeals record that can be
tidied up afterwards is not a record. Admins are notified on arrival,
the participant on the answer.

Re-assessment (5.50). ac_reassessment_requests, raisable by an assessor
as well as an admin, and declined is a first-class outcome: we offered
and they said no is the part that gets questioned later.

The decision (5.9). candidates.decision_outcome/_made_at/_note, plus
decision_communicated_at, which is the clause. VIFM does not decide;
this records what the client decided so the participant can be told,
and says so in the UI. Telling someone with no portal account reports
that they still need telling directly.

The report's challenge paragraph now points at the portal route, and
the three sample PDFs are regenerated with it.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Tell the truth when a demo load changes nothing
entries.plain: Demo loads now clearly show whether data was actually reloaded or left unchanged, so you know whether a refresh actually happened.
entries.explanation:
Every service seeder skips itself when its demo rows already exist, so
loading on top of loaded data is a no-op. The page reported all of it in
green under a success toast, which is how a demo that had not been
refreshed came to look exactly like one that had.

A service that created nothing is now amber and reads 'unchanged', and a
load where nothing at all happened warns instead of congratulating. The
operation people actually want after a seeder change is a rebuild, so
that is now the primary button once demo data is present, with the
top-up load kept beside it as 'Load missing services'.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Fix two gaps found reviewing the live Assessment Center screens
entries.plain: Assessor names in conflict-of-interest dropdown now include email addresses to prevent selecting the wrong person, and demo data now includes assessment purpose.
entries.explanation:
The conflict-of-interest dropdown listed two assessors with the same
display name and no way to tell them apart. Two real accounts share
"Dr. Sarah Al Ameri", so declaring a conflict against the wrong one would
have left the actual conflict unenforced. The option now carries the email.

The demo seeder created its engagement with no purpose, so every
demonstration showed "Purpose: Not recorded" and fell back to a consensus
overall rating - the behaviour phase 1 changed. The demo engagement now
models a selection centre: purpose set, weights confirmed, a participant
contact, and other methods marked context only.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Assessment Center: phase 1 of the BPS standard gap closure
entries.plain: Assessment centre records now show the purpose of each evaluation and calculate overall ratings using a standardized, transparent method.
entries.explanation:
Measured against the BPS Division of Occupational Psychology standard for
the design and delivery of assessment centres. This closes the phase 1
items; the register and build plan list the rest.

Purpose and integration (3.7, 4.34, 4.35, 7.1-7.6, 8.2)
  An engagement now records what it is for. A selection centre reaches its
  overall rating by weighted average of the agreed competency ratings,
  computed server-side so the browser's number is ignored, with the decimal
  kept and the inputs stored so the figure can be reconstructed. The panel
  may record disagreement; the calculation stands. Development centres keep
  the consensus. No arithmetic rating is produced until a person confirms
  the weights, since weights nobody approved would be worse than the
  consensus they replace.

Staffing (4.16, 4.17, 5.15-5.21, 5.32, 5.36)
  More than one assessor per participant and one per three are enforced at
  activation, overridable only with a recorded reason. Conflicts of interest
  are declared per pair and refuse assignment. Assessor load is reported.

Reports (5.43, 5.49, 8.2, 8.6, 8.8-8.12, 8.20)
  Every report ends with what it may be used for, what it cannot tell you,
  its technical quality, a named contact and how to challenge a result. The
  technical-quality line reads the real SME approval count, so it changes as
  the review lands. Releasing a report records who checked it.

Delivery and other methods (4.32, 6.7-6.13)
  An immutable log of what happened during a centre and what was done about
  it. Each centre records whether results from tests, questionnaires or 360s
  may move a rating, shown to assessors at the wash-up.

Also: the demo seeder provisions a three-assessor panel so demos pass the new
staffing rules, and the sample reports are regenerated. Fixed while reviewing
them: the summary page called a calculated rating a consensus, the
recommendation tile clipped long values, and "0 development needs" sat beside
two named development areas without saying they were simply the lowest rated.

Migrations 00204-00209, applied and verified on production.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: VAT 5%/15% + WHT 15% tax treatment option
entries.plain: Proposals can now include VAT and withholding tax options, with automatically calculated totals and appropriate legal wording for your region.
entries.explanation:
"Tax treatment" select on the builder (licenceData bag, no migration):
- VAT 5% (UAE) / VAT 15% (KSA): a VAT line + VAT-inclusive grand total
  render after the commercial tables (all pricing modes + financial
  variant), the exec-summary Total investment shows the inclusive figure,
  and the "exclusive of any applicable taxes" boilerplate flips to
  inclusive-of-VAT wording. EN + AR.
- WHT 15%: totals stay gross; an explicit note states the client may
  deduct 15% withholding at source, and the fees sentence says gross of
  WHT. EN + AR.
The DB total stays pre-tax (ARR metrics unaffected); VAT is computed at
render time, so the Word export inherits it too.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Add public ARC organizational dashboard sample page
entries.plain: A sample AI-readiness dashboard is now available as a shareable, branded page that prospects can explore without needing special access.
entries.explanation:
Serves the interactive AI-readiness org dashboard (drill Overall -> Division
-> Department -> Individual, EN/AR toggle) as a branded, shareable link at
/samples/arc-dashboard. Self-contained static demo with clearly-labelled
sample data - no PII, no data fetch. Route handler returns the file that also
lives under public/samples/; middleware bypasses auth for /samples/*.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Scientific Models: sample reports for Leadership, DARE, EQ too
entries.plain: Sample reports are now available for Leadership, DARE, and EQ assessments to help clients see what results look like.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Scientific Models: downloadable HiPo sample report from the platform
entries.plain: Admins can now download a sample High-Potential report directly from the platform to review assessment output quality.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Platform Clients: per-row Edit dialog (rename across both org stores)
entries.plain: Client records can now be renamed directly from a quick edit dialog that updates the name across your entire system.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: fix engagement breakdown lost on reload/edit (combined + engagement)
entries.plain: Proposals with engagement pricing breakdowns no longer lose their details when you reload or re-edit them.
entries.explanation:
A saved combined/engagement proposal persists its engagement in the
normalized {groups} shape, but the read paths only looked for the input
shape (engagements[] / legacy) - never groups. So on reload the engagement
re-read as empty and its whole pricing breakdown was dropped from the
report (the frozen total still included it). The builder had the same blind
spot and, worse, fell back to the starter template - re-saving silently
overwrote the real engagement with template numbers.

- rawGroupsFrom() reads groups -> engagements -> legacy, used by
  normalizeEngagementModel + withEngagementResidency (server render path).
- Builder seedGroups reads em.groups first, mirroring the same priority, so
  editing a saved proposal loads the real engagement, not the template.
- withEngagementResidency strips a previously-baked residency line before
  re-adding, so duplicating/re-pricing a fee-only engagement can't
  double-count the residency fee.

Read-path fix, no migration: existing proposals show the full breakdown on
the next render. Verified: reload renders, fee-only residency counts once,
normal engagement keeps its lines.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: revocable client link, honest pricing box, full-set KPIs
entries.plain: Client proposal links are now automatically revoked when marked lost, pricing is accurately displayed, and all KPIs appear in reports.
entries.explanation:
Proposals review (no XSS, no admin IDOR - all commercial/data-integrity):

Client token surface (major):
- The client page + PDF + Word only excluded 'draft', so a withdrawn/
  superseded ('lost') proposal stayed served with no revoke. Gate on an
  issued/won allowlist (isProposalClientVisible), so marking a proposal
  'lost' revokes its client link - the module's only revoke lever.
- Enforce valid_until: an expired OUTSTANDING ('issued') offer renders a
  short "expired" notice and 404s its downloads. A 'won' deal is closed, so
  its offer-validity is moot and it stays viewable (the renewal flow
  re-points won clients here long after that date).
- The generic Subtotal / "Discount (X%)" / Total box was only coherent for
  per-project pricing; for licence/combined/engagement it mislabelled the
  discount and total could exceed subtotal. Show the itemised box only for
  per-project; other modes show the correct Total + point to the PDF.

Backend correctness:
- loadProposals (list + ARR/win-rate dashboard) was .limit(500); paginate
  so the KPIs cover every proposal. Renewal cron read paginated too.
- Clamp stored discount_pct to 0-100 (the amount was already clamped).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Revert "Auth: lock down /register (provision-only platform, no self-signup)"
entries.plain: Self-signup registration restrictions have been removed to restore normal account access.
entries.explanation: This reverts commit 5e08adbe1937e7d777c1b101be02111a2b91ec2d.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Auth: lock down /register (provision-only platform, no self-signup)
entries.plain: The registration page now directs users to login since all accounts are created by admins, not self-service.
entries.explanation:
Caliber has no self-service sign-up - every account is created by an admin
(create-admin.ts / provision-candidate / provision-client-manager / the
in-app Invite to portal button); there is no public auth.signUp path. The
/register route was a dead placeholder that still invited prospects to
"create an account" they cannot. Redirect it to /login instead.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: AC core: wash-up edit-loss guard, integration upsert, atomic create
entries.plain: Multi-user assessments now warn before overwriting unsaved scores, and integration data saves fail safely instead of losing information.
entries.explanation:
- Wash-up (Realtime, the multi-user differentiator): a colleague's save could
  silently overwrite the score/notes an assessor was mid-typing. Now a
  per-competency dirty tracker keeps unsaved local edits and warns instead of
  clobbering, with per-competency own-echo tokens (added only on save success)
  so a failed save can never misclassify a colleague's change as our own.
- Integration worksheet: the non-atomic delete-then-insert (a failed insert
  after a successful delete destroyed the saved rating) is now a single atomic
  upsert on the natural key (migration 00189 unique index; dedupe-then-index,
  applied + verified).
- Engagement creation: the non-atomic 4-step multi-insert with error-swallowing
  manual rollback now delegates to the create_engagement_atomic RPC (one
  transaction) via the service client, gated on admin (it bypasses RLS). 00188's
  now-stale "app does not call this RPC" note corrected.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: AC core: honest ICC/bias stats + 1000-row pagination sweep
entries.plain: Rater agreement and bias statistics now calculate accurately per assessment instead of inflating numbers across mixed groups.
entries.explanation:
Analytics + scoring correctness:
- ICC was pooled across ALL engagements with missing rater cells imputed
  as the subject mean - manufacturing agreement and inflating the number.
  Rebuilt per-engagement, complete-case: each engagement contributes its
  best co-rating rater pair (no imputation, no cross-engagement pooling),
  weighted by subject count; null (honest "insufficient data") when no
  genuinely double-rated block exists.
- "Halo effect" measured pooled modal concentration (duplicating central
  tendency); now measures real within-candidate cross-competency agreement
  (population SD on the 1-5 scale, bounded [0,1]).

1000-row cap sweep (any unpaginated select silently truncates at 1000,
corrupting cohort-scaled reads). New fetchAllByIdChunks helper (chunk the
id list + page within each chunk) plus fetchAllPages applied to:
- admin analytics (ratings/candidates/OARs/consensus feeding ICC + bias)
- admin engagement detail (assignments + integration worksheets)
- wash-up progress (consensus - undercounted the progress bars)
- retention purge (id-gather paginated + delete chunked, so a backlog
  > 1000 fully purges instead of leaving the rest over-retained)
- candidate report PDF (observations)
- client engagement matrix, client analytics, client reports

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: AC core: authorize + freeze assessor write paths (IDOR + immutability)
entries.plain: Assessors can no longer edit ratings or final scores for candidates outside their own engagement, protecting data security.
entries.explanation:
The assessor pipeline authorized writes by ROLE only, then wrote via the
service client (bypassing RLS) using client-supplied ids - so any
authenticated assessor could clobber the ratings/consensus/final OAR
(which feed client reports + ac_ready_now credentials) of any candidate
in any other client's engagement.

- New src/lib/ac/assessor-guards.ts: requireAssessorForEngagement /
  requireAssignmentOwner / assertCandidateInEngagement /
  assertCompetencyInEngagement / assertEngagementUnlocked.
- Wash-up consensus + OAR: require assessor-assigned-to-engagement +
  candidate-in-engagement + competency-in-scope + not-finalised.
- Observation/rating writes + deletes: require assignment ownership +
  not-finalised (resolve observation->assignment before delete-by-id).
- Integration worksheet: derive assessor_id from the session so a real
  assessor can't spoof authorship or delete a colleague's row.
- CBI approve-to-pipeline: honour the same finalisation freeze (it writes
  the same observations/ratings tables).
- Immutability: writes are frozen once the engagement is completed/archived
  (report released + credential issued).
- Migration 00188: lock down the unused create_engagement_atomic SECURITY
  DEFINER RPC - pin search_path, REVOKE public/anon/authenticated EXECUTE,
  grant only service_role. Applied + verified (anon/auth EXECUTE = false).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Item banks: honest badge - fixed content in review is not vetted
entries.plain: A badge now clearly marks test content under review as not yet verified by quality control.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: technical/financial split, one-price all-solutions, editable Word export
entries.plain: Proposals now show technical and financial details separately, offer a single price for all solutions, and let you edit Word exports.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: KAFD feedback - solution wording, section 19 sample reports, currency picker
entries.plain: Proposals now include improved solution descriptions, section 19 sample reports, and a currency selector for international use.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Item banks: "Send all back to review" bulk action per bank
entries.plain: Subject matter experts can now send an entire test bank back for review in one click to make bulk edits before re-approval.
entries.explanation:
The inverse of the bulk-approve: un-approve a whole bank's approved/live
pool in one click so an SME can review + edit before re-approving.

- reopenBankForReviewAction(key) (admin-gated, service-role): status-only
  updates per table - persona/logica/techno/prehire -> in_review or
  pending, fluent live -> in_review, ARC approved -> pending
- two-click confirm ReopenButton on each reopenable bank card
  (persona/logica/techno/prehire/fluent/arc), shown only when the bank
  has approved content
- reopening un-serves the vetted bank until re-approved (falls back to
  live-AI, results flagged provisional again) - the honest trade-off

Verified: dashboard renders 200, 6 buttons, no client/server boundary
error, tsc + lint clean.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Persona + Fluent banks: inline item editing in the SME console
entries.plain: Persona and Fluent test items can now be edited directly in the admin console instead of only being approved or rejected.
entries.explanation:
The Persona and Fluent consoles only had approve/reject/retire - no way
to edit an item's wording once approved. Add inline editors (the other
four banks already have them).

- Persona: edit EN/AR text + reverse-keyed flag; editing returns the
  item to 'pending' (re-approval required)
- Fluent: edit receptive items (passage/script + question + 4 options +
  correct index) and productive prompts (EN/AR); editing returns the
  item to 'in_review' for re-promotion
- updatePersonaItemAction / updateFluentItemAction (admin-gated,
  service-role); both re-open review on edit so an approval never
  silently covers changed wording

Verified: both consoles render 200, no client/server boundary error,
tsc + lint clean.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Pre-Hire quiz bank: SME review console (/admin/quiz-bank)
entries.plain: Pre-Hire quiz bank now has a review console where Subject Matter Experts can approve, reject, or retire individual test questions before they go live.
entries.explanation:
The approval UI that activates the competency quiz bank. Per-competency cards
show approved vs in-review counts; "Approve all in review" is the SME batch
sign-off (a competency serves from the bank once it clears 8 approved). Per-item
approve / reject / retire / Arabic-review, two-person review enforced on approve
(approver != drafter, dev-bypassed), edit-resets-to-in_review.

- src/lib/quiz-bank/admin.ts: loadCompetencyQuizBank (per-competency counts+items)
- src/app/admin/quiz-bank: page + console + server actions
- nav link "Quiz Bank"; readiness dashboard "manage" link -> /admin/quiz-bank

Verified E2E on the live bank: approve -> 10 servable items + working exposure
RPC + readiness counts the competency servable -> revert restores in_review.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: pipeline dashboard by status
entries.plain: New proposals dashboard shows you every deal at a glance - broken down by draft, sent, won, and lost - with totals, values, and win rates.
entries.explanation:
New /admin/proposals/dashboard giving a pipeline view of every proposal
by status - draft, sent (issued), won, lost.

- Headline metrics: total proposals, open pipeline value (draft + sent),
  won value, win rate (won / decided)
- Four status cards (count + value) with a by-status donut and the ARR
  footnote (sent + won licences)
- A table per status listing its proposals (title, client, total, type,
  created/sent date), so you can see exactly what is in each bucket;
  titles link to the proposal
- "Dashboard" link added to the proposals list header

Values summed in the dominant currency across proposals.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: rich-text section editing + no blank sections
entries.plain: Proposal sections now have formatting tools (bold, italics, colours) and all 19 sections can be edited with actual content instead of staying blank.
entries.explanation:
Every one of the 19 sections is now edited with a rich-text toolbar
(bold, italic, underline, text colour, font size), and the previously
blank computed sections show editable prose.

- RichTextEditor: a lightweight contentEditable + toolbar; emits HTML
- rich-text.ts: strict sanitize-html allowlist (inline formatting only -
  scripts/handlers/style/iframe stripped). Applied on save AND on render
  (defence in depth), since the HTML flows into the Puppeteer PDF
- Renderer override path injects sanitised HTML (legacy plain-text
  overrides still fall back to the markdown-lite path)
- Section editor pre-fills each box with the section's default body as
  sanitised HTML, so it shows formatted; edit replaces, Reset restores
- Computed sections (Commercial pricing, Psychometric evidence,
  Implementation timeline, Evidence samples) now expose their intro
  PROSE (editable, pre-filled -> never blank) with the table kept
  generated below, so a text edit never freezes the live pricing/evidence

Verified live: toolbar formats text; save -> PDF/Word carry the bold /
colour / size; a <script> in the content is stripped end-to-end; the
pricing table stays live under an edited Commercial prose; EN + AR both
render. Adds the sanitize-html dependency.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: edit every section's wording on the proposal page
entries.plain: You can now edit the wording of every section in your proposal directly on the proposal page, and only your changes save - everything else updates automatically.
entries.explanation:
After Create, the proposal page now lists every section with its current
wording and an Edit toggle that opens EN + Arabic boxes pre-filled with
that text. Only sections you actually change are stored as overrides;
untouched sections stay dynamic (client name, totals and pricing tables
keep auto-updating). Then Download PDF/Word reflects the edits.

- Renderers expose each section's default body (proposalSectionDefaults);
  section-editor.ts extracts it to editable markdown-lite for the pre-fill
- New ProposalSectionEditor on /admin/proposals/[id]; the builder's old
  override panel is removed (superseded) and collapsed under pricing
- Table-bearing sections (Implementation plan, licence-mode Proposed
  solution, Commercial, Definitions, Terms, Acceptance, etc.) are prepend:
  the box is an intro above the generated table, which is never destroyed
- saveProposalSections merges into licence_data.sectionOverrides (no
  re-pricing); preserves overrides for excluded sections; updateProposal
  read-merges sectionOverrides so a pricing save can't clobber them
- Editor is resilient to the included-section set growing after mount

Adversarially reviewed (4 dimensions + verify); the 2 major + 3 minor
findings from that pass are fixed and verified live (edit->save->reload,
untouched-stays-dynamic, PDF/Word EN+AR, table-section intro-note, and
the section-set-growth no-crash case).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: combined pricing mode (services + engagement)
entries.plain: Proposals can now mix service pricing and consultant engagements in one quote, each with its own subtotal and a combined total.
entries.explanation:
A new `combined` pricing mode lets one proposal hold per-seat services
(or an annual licence) PLUS one or more consultant engagements, each
itemised under its own subtotal with a single combined grand total.

- Migration 00178 widens the pricing_mode CHECK to admit 'combined'
- service.ts prices the services block (per-project or licence) and the
  engagement block, concatenates line items, and adds data residency
  exactly once (on the services block, never double-counted)
- EN + AR renders: combined Commercial section, proposed-solution,
  exec-summary facts, cover subtitle and intro
- Builder gains a Combined toggle with a "price services as" sub-toggle
  (per project / annual licence / engagement only) plus a live
  combined-total preview; save writes both models + combinedServicesMode

Verified end-to-end on the live DB (migration applied, combined save
round-trips, detail page renders the combined total).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: multiple engagements, Word download, cover cleanup
entries.plain: Proposals now support multiple consultant engagements, and you can download them as Word documents as well as PDFs, in English and Arabic.
entries.explanation:
- Engagement mode supports multiple named engagements, each a block of
  line items, all itemised in the financial proposal (per-engagement
  subtotal + combined grand total). Backward compatible with existing
  single-engagement proposals; no migration (engagement_model jsonb).
- Word (.doc) download alongside PDF on both admin + client surfaces
  (EN + AR), reusing the same HTML builders wrapped for MS Word.
- Remove the contact person name from the cover (hero + metadata panel),
  EN + AR - client org, city/country and email only.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: data residency as a real pricing line item
entries.plain: Data residency costs now appear as a real pricing line item that discounts and totals like everything else, instead of being tacked on at the end.
entries.explanation:
Move the data-residency cost from a bolt-on fee (after the subtotal)
into a genuine line item in the pricing model:
- per-project + engagement: a pre-subtotal line, injected at compute
  time (never persisted, so editing never duplicates it), so it flows
  through subtotal -> discount -> total like any other line.
- licence: a one-time line in the fee build-up (into Year-1 + 3-yr TCO),
  kept out of the bundle-discounted a-la-carte pool - discounting or
  annualising a one-time infra cost would misprice it.
Flat lines show a dash for the per-participant columns. EN + AR.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: data-residency choice on all pricing modes
entries.plain: You can now choose where your data lives - Saudi Arabia, UAE, or VIFM-managed cloud - on any pricing type, and this choice appears in the proposal.
entries.explanation:
Add a proposal-level Data Residency selector (Saudi Arabia / UAE /
VIFM-managed cloud) shown in the builder for every pricing mode, not
just engagement. Stored in the existing licence_data jsonb (no
migration); defaults to VIFM for existing proposals.

Renders a "Data residency" statement in the proposed-solution section
of every proposal - per-project, licence and engagement - in EN and
Arabic (in-country sovereign for KSA/UAE; managed cloud for VIFM).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: redesign PDF cover + client city/country
entries.plain: Proposals now have a premium redesigned cover with a navy gradient and modern design, and you can add the client's city and country.
entries.explanation:
Premium bilingual proposal cover: layered navy gradient, dot-grid
texture, bolder V motif, accent title spine, glassy metadata panel.
Leads with the offer and the client name (no pricing on the cover).
Arabic cover fully RTL-mirrored to match.

Add optional client city + country (migration 00177), surfaced as a
"City, Country" line under the client name. Editable in the builder,
persisted on create/update with independent column-peel tolerance,
and carried through duplicate-as-revision.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: engagement (professional-services) pricing mode - Assessment Center
entries.plain: Proposals can now be priced as professional services engagements - perfect for Assessment Center projects where you charge for consultant time and days, not just seats.
entries.explanation:
The Assessment Center is a consultant-led engagement, not a per-seat product: its
cost is dominated by consultant time (assessor days + 1:1 feedback) plus fixed
design/reporting fees. Neither per-project (seats x rate) nor licence (annual SaaS)
expresses that, so this adds a third pricing mode - "engagement" - a flexible
professional-services line-item quote.

- New pure engine engagement.ts: EngagementLine { label, basis, quantity, unitRate }
  where basis is fixed / per_participant / per_day (consultant-day) / per_session
  (per-delegate feedback); computeEngagement sums line totals -> subtotal ->
  discount -> total. acEngagementTemplate() seeds the standard AC quote (design +
  per-participant + assessor-days ~1/2 delegates + feedback + cohort report),
  scaling quantities off the participant count. Rates are editable placeholders.
- Migration 00176: widens the pricing_mode CHECK to add 'engagement' + an
  engagement_model jsonb snapshot column. NOT applied here (reviewable branch).
- service.ts: engagement branch in buildPricedSnapshot (derives scope/line_items/
  rollups from the lines); engagement_model joins the column-peel ladder; a save
  without 00176 fails loud ("apply migration 00176"), never silently.
- proposal-html.ts + proposal-html-ar.ts: engagement commercial line-item table +
  an AC methodology "how it runs" solution block (exercises -> assessor observation
  -> wash-up/OAR -> feedback -> reporting) + engagement exec intro, in EN and RTL AR.
- Builder: a third "Engagement" toggle with a line-item editor (label + basis +
  qty + rate + amount, add/remove), a "Load Assessment Center template" button,
  participants + engagement-name fields, and a live total. List-page chip gains
  "Engagement".

tsc + lint clean; engine ($23,600 AC template), EN + AR PDF render, and builder
compile all verified.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: roll renewal-reminder date to the next anniversary (review fix)
entries.plain: Licence renewal reminders now fire correctly every year instead of only once, so no contracts slip through without notice.
entries.explanation:
The renewal cron computed base + 1 year as a fixed date, so it only ever fired
for the Year-1->2 anniversary and skipped every later cycle (and a freshly-issued
licence with a future base window). Roll the date forward year-by-year to the
next anniversary at/after (now - 30d) so every renewal cycle is caught and a
day-one licence is never nagged.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals Phase 4: SaaS lifecycle - ARR tile, renewal cron, duplicate-as-revision
entries.plain: The proposals list now shows annual revenue from active licences, and you can create a new revision of any proposal that automatically updates pricing.
entries.explanation:
- ARR tile row on the proposals list: annual recurring revenue summed across
  issued/won licence proposals (via computeLicensing), plus active-licence and
  won counts. Verified rendering on live data.
- Duplicate-as-revision: duplicateAsRevision() in service.ts copies a proposal
  into a new draft numbered "(rev N)" linked via revision_of_id (root resolved so
  revisions of revisions chain to the original); re-prices from the current rate
  card / stored licence model. duplicateAsRevisionAction + a "Duplicate as
  revision" button on the detail page. revision_of_id persists via the peel ladder.
- Licence renewal reminders: /api/proposals/admin/renewals/cron (Bearer
  CRON_SECRET, timing-safe) sweeps issued/won licence proposals whose 12-month
  renewal (issued/sent + 1yr) is within 60 days, emails proposal_renewal_reminder,
  and dedups via licence_data.renewalNoticeSentAt (~10-month window). New
  proposal_renewal_reminder email template + .github/workflows/
  proposal-renewal-reminders.yml (daily 07:00 UTC, clones the Reflect cron). Fully
  tolerant of the licence columns being absent.

Phase 4 of the TI-merge follow-ups. tsc + lint clean; ARR render + cron auth gate verified.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals Phase 3: bilingual EN/AR proposal render
entries.plain: Proposals now generate in full Arabic, right-to-left, with all sections, pricing, and terms in Arabic alongside English.
entries.explanation:
- New proposal-html-ar.ts: a full Arabic (RTL) mirror of the proposal PDF -
  cover, contents, all sections (respecting section selection + tiers), the
  licence build-up + multi-year + pilot, SaaS T&C clauses, definitions, ROI
  paragraph, live evidence and the evidence appendix. Numbers, money and
  percentages are wrapped dir="ltr" so bidi keeps them readable in the RTL flow;
  numbering/TOC/clause-counter derive from the same included-section set as EN.
- Both PDF routes accept ?language=ar and dispatch to the Arabic builder, with an
  -AR filename suffix and an Arabic footer label; EN remains the default.
- Download affordances: an Arabic-PDF button on the admin detail page and on the
  client token view (alongside the English download).
- Arabic content is MSA, best-effort pending human review (project convention).
  Uses the Noto Naskh webfont (same as the 5 existing AR reports); render
  verified (14-page RTL PDF, LTR-wrapped figures, licence build-up in Arabic).

Phase 3 of the TI-merge follow-ups. tsc + lint clean.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: annual all-access licence pricing mode (TI merge Phase 1)
entries.plain: Proposals can now be priced as an annual all-access Caliber licence instead of just a one-off project, with bundle discounts and multi-year options.
entries.explanation:
Grafts the VIFM Proposals Portal's SaaS licence commercial model onto
Caliber's proposal generator, per the Talent Intelligence merge handover.
Proposals now price EITHER as a one-off project (seats x rate, unchanged)
or as a committed annual all-access Caliber licence, chosen via a toggle
that defaults new proposals to licence mode.

- New pure engine src/lib/proposals/licensing.ts (normalizeLicensingModel +
  computeLicensing): a-la-carte -> bundle discount -> licence -> +support% ->
  +sovereign -> annual recurring -> +one-time -> Year-1 -> Y2/Y3 -> 3-yr TCO,
  plus usage buffer and an optional pilot with conversion credit. Verified
  against the handover worked example ($276k -> $224,374 Year-1, $470,565 TCO).
- Migration 00175 adds pricing_mode / licensing_model / section_selection /
  revision_of_id / licence_data to proposals and seeds the rate card with the
  benchmark unit prices. NOT applied here (reviewable branch).
- service.ts writes tolerate an un-applied 00175 via a column-peel ladder:
  per-project rows peel the new columns and save as today; licence rows never
  peel them, so a licence save without 00175 fails loud instead of silently
  writing a per-project row. Licence mode derives scope/line_items/rollups from
  the licence build-up so every scope-driven PDF section keeps working.
- proposal-html.ts renders the licence build-up, committed-scope table, buffer
  note, multi-year TCO, pilot, agreed SLA figures, SaaS T&C clauses (16.11-15)
  and licence definitions - all gated on licence mode; per-project output is
  byte-identical. Section count stays 18 so the TOC / clause numbering is stable.
- Builder gains the mode toggle, editable per-service unit prices, a licence
  parameters card (discount / support / implementation / tier / buffer / uplift
  / pilot) and a live build-up box. List page shows a Licence/Project chip.

Phase 1 of 5. Follow-ups: EN/AR licence render, ARR tile + renewal cron,
section-selection UI, evidence appendix.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: VIFM Brand Kit compliance (logos + Open Sans)
entries.plain: Proposal PDFs now follow VIFM's brand guidelines, using the correct logos and Open Sans font on the right coloured backgrounds.
entries.explanation:
Aligns the proposal PDF with the VIFM Brand Kit. The monochrome white logo
now sits on the dark navy cover and the primary color logo on the light
Contents page (per the kit's dark/light background rules - no effects, clear
space respected). Logos embed as cached data URIs via the new
src/lib/proposals/logo.ts (Puppeteer setContent can't resolve /public URLs);
a missing file degrades to no logo rather than failing the PDF. The document
also now loads Open Sans (the kit's primary font) via webfont instead of
silently falling back to Arial. Palette was already brand-aligned
(#010131 / #5391D5 / #111232).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: full professional business-proposal PDF (12 sections + legal + signatures)
entries.plain: Proposals are now complete 8-page professional business documents with branded covers, company information, and legal details instead of simple 2-page quotes.
entries.explanation:
The proposal PDF was a compact 2-page quote. It is now a complete 8-page
business document: branded cover (reference number VIFM-P-YYYY-XXXXXX,
confidentiality notice), contents page, and 12 numbered sections - executive
summary with key-facts strip, About VIFM, understanding of requirements
(client/sector/region aware), proposed solution with per-service deliverables,
methodology & quality standards (ISO 10667 / ITF-6 alignment), phased
implementation plan, project governance, data protection & security
(UAE PDPL / Saudi PDPL / GDPR), commercial proposal with included/excluded,
assumptions & exclusions, ten numbered T&C clauses (confidentiality, IP,
liability cap, termination, force majeure, governing law resolved from the
client's region), and an acceptance page with dual signature blocks.

Supporting changes: per-service PROPOSAL_DELIVERABLES catalogue;
renderHtmlToPdfBuffer gains an optional running page footer ("Page N of M" +
reference) used by both proposal PDF routes; validity dates pinned to noon
UTC so the legal date can never drift a day with server timezone (PDF +
client view).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposals: in-page PDF download with progress (no more blank tab)
entries.plain: PDF proposals now download smoothly with a progress indicator instead of opening a blank screen in a new browser tab.
entries.explanation:
Download PDF was a bare target=_blank link to the Puppeteer route. Chromium
takes 2-5s to render the PDF on Render, so the new tab sat on the browser's
dark, empty PDF-viewer shell with zero feedback - reported as "a dark blank
screen" (and embedded previews cannot open _blank tabs at all).

New shared PdfDownloadButton fetches the PDF in-page, shows a disabled
"Preparing PDF..." spinner state while the server renders, then saves the
file with a proper VIFM-Proposal-<client>.pdf name; failures surface a real
error message instead of a stranded tab. Wired into both the admin proposal
actions and the client proposal view.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proposal generator: rate card + builder + PDF + client portal + email
entries.plain: You can now build, price, and send professional proposals directly within Caliber with automatic service pricing and client access links.
entries.explanation:
A native talent-intelligence proposal generator inside Caliber (V1, EN).

- Migration 00174: proposal_rates (per-service per-seat rate card, seeded for
  the 7 services, USD default) + proposals (snapshotted scope + line items +
  totals + unguessable client access_token). Admin RLS; client reads by token.
- Auto-assembly: /admin/proposals/new builds a proposal from a selected client
  and optional Bespoke bundle (prefills services + scope), with a headcount per
  service. Pricing derives from seats x the rate card; snapshotted on save so a
  later rate change never alters an issued proposal.
- Technical section reuses each instrument's methodology framing; commercials
  render a line-item table. Caliber-branded A4 PDF via renderHtmlToPdfBuffer.
- Client delivery: token-gated /proposals/[token] view + PDF (issued only,
  auth-bypassed in middleware) and an "Email proposal" action that attaches the
  PDF (new proposal_delivery template) and marks the proposal issued.
- Admin: list, rate-card editor, builder (create + edit), detail with
  download / send / status. Sidebar link under Platform.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Fix Register: plain-English explanation for every change
entries.plain: All platform changes now display in plain language first, with technical details available for those who need them.
entries.explanation:
Every entry now leads with a jargon-free sentence a non-technical reader can
understand (what changed and why it matters), with the raw commit message
tucked behind a "Technical detail" expander.

- scripts/explain-fix-register.mjs: AI-writes one plain sentence per commit
  (Haiku, batched), cached by hash in src/data/fix-register-explanations.json.
  Incremental (only uncached commits) + crash-safe + tolerant (no key / model
  error just leaves the raw message as fallback). 597/600 seeded.
- Generator merges the cache as `plain` on each entry.
- prebuild runs generate -> explain -> generate so new commits are explained
  on each deploy.
- Page: plain line is the headline; a "What the labels mean" legend explains
  Critical / Security / Audit / Fix / Feature / Change in plain terms.
- Per-service list capped at 20 with a "Show more" expander (lighter render).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Add live Fix Register admin page (per-service, git-derived)
entries.plain: Administrators can now view a live changelog showing every update to Caliber, organized by feature, with dates and authors.
entries.explanation:
A live, admin-only changelog at /admin/fix-register showing, per service,
every change shipped to Caliber with its fix date, author, optional
requester, and full explanation.

- scripts/generate-fix-register.mjs parses the commit history, classifies
  each commit to a service by touched files + message, infers a change
  type, and extracts an optional "Requested-by:" trailer. Writes
  src/data/fix-register.generated.json. Tolerant of no .git at build.
- Wired into "prebuild" so the register refreshes on every deploy; also
  runnable via "npm run gen:fix-register".
- Page is a server component + client filter (search, service, type).
  Admin-only for free under the /admin layout role gate.
- Sidebar link under Platform.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Add Caliber marketing landing page at root (dual-mode: public landing / staff launcher)
entries.plain: The platform now has a professional marketing landing page at the home URL that shows services to visitors and acts as a staff launcher when logged in.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Framework PDF: drop behavioural indicators, keep definitions only
entries.plain: The framework PDF now shows competency definitions without the detailed behavioural indicators, keeping documents more concise.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Licensed Preview: logo, per-sector tuning, lead modules, shareable link
entries.plain: Licensed previews now display an organization logo, customize headlines and scoring by industry, highlight key modules, and can be shared via a read-only public link.
entries.explanation: 1) Logo URL on the launcher (falls back to initials). 2) Per-sector headline/tagline + score bias so a bank's tenant differs from a ministry's. 3) Lead-module picker -> a Spotlight nav group + Featured cards. 4) Public read-only shareable link at /share/preview (middleware-bypassed, shareMode hides admin Exit) as a prospect leave-behind. Shared param parser; logo restricted to http(s).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Persist voucher client contact to the DB on all 7 portals
entries.plain: When issuing vouchers across all assessment types, the system now saves the contact person's name, title, and email address with each voucher.
entries.explanation: Migration 00168 adds contact_name/title/email to every *_vouchers table (+ client_name/project_label/expires_at on rr_vouchers). All 7 insert libs + their actions + UIs thread the step-1 contact through, so it's stored on each issued voucher. Inserts peel the new columns on a schema-cache miss for fresh-env tolerance.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Standardize step-1 voucher details across all 7 portals
entries.plain: All voucher issuance forms now ask for the same details in step one - client name, project label, expiry date, and contact information - for consistency.
entries.explanation: Shared VoucherDetailsFields: Client name, Project label, Expiry, Contact name/title/email in step 1 of every wizard; contact prefills the step-3 email-to-client. RR gains a Details step + emails the shared link to the contact.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Add unified dark voucher header + service tabs
entries.plain: All assessment services now share a consistent dark header and tab design, so staff navigate between Fluent, Logica, Persona, Techno, ARC, Pre-Hire, and Role Readiness the same way everywhere.
entries.explanation: Shared VoucherNav (VIFM - VOUCHERS / Issue vouchers dark bar + pill tabs for Fluent/Logica/Persona/Techno/ARC/Pre-Hire/Role Readiness) on each voucher page; the /admin/vouchers hub gets the same dark header + pill tabs.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Pre-Hire audit B2.5: token-scope API bypass, dedupe stage plan
entries.plain: Security and accuracy improvements: Pre-Hire now prevents unauthorized API access and stops duplicate assessment stages from skewing results, while making AI-generated scores clearly visible to reviewers.
entries.explanation:
Tighten /api/prehire auth-bypass to a UUID-shaped token segment so a
future non-token route under the prefix can't be silently public (I-3).
Reject duplicate stage kinds in a requisition's stage plan, which would
double-count a stage's weight in the composite (S-8). Surface the
AI-draft nature of per-stage + CBI scores on the SME review page and
switch its inline back link to the shared BackLink (UA-1/2/3).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Role Readiness: combined candidate sitting + report + middleware
entries.plain: Role Readiness assessments can now be taken by candidates, scored automatically, and reported with personalized development plans - completing the end-to-end assessment experience.
entries.explanation:
- sitting.ts: serves Persona items scoped to the role's competencies (reuses the
  behavioural engine), grades the Techno-style technical MCQs server-side
  (answer key never sent), writes per-section results + finalizes the verdict.
- report-data.ts: shared result/report builder (per-side scores, per-competency +
  per-area breakdown, dev plan from below-target items with SME-editable text).
- 7 candidate API routes under /api/role-readiness/[token] (consent, persona
  start/submit, technical start/submit, result, report PDF) + the apply UI
  (/role-readiness/apply/[token]) with consent -> Persona Likert -> Techno MCQ ->
  on-screen verdict + dev plan + PDF download.
- role-readiness-html.ts: Puppeteer A4 report, inline SVG + CSS only.
- middleware: auth-bypass the token candidate + API routes.
tsc + lint clean.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Client portal: bounce a logged-in client_manager off public marketing pages
entries.plain: Client managers are now automatically redirected away from public marketing pages, keeping them confined to their client portal once they log in.
entries.explanation:
The AI Readiness landing (/ara), /courses and /evidence were auth-bypassed,
so a signed-in client_manager could still view them. Now those marketing
pages run redirectIfClientManager first: anonymous prospects + VIFM staff
see them unchanged, but a client_manager is redirected to /portal - so the
manager is fully confined to their portal.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Client portal: confine client_manager to /portal (dim + block)
entries.plain: Client managers can no longer access other parts of the platform by typing URLs - they are locked to their portal, and unavailable services are grayed out to show what their company hasn't purchased.
entries.explanation:
A client_manager landed on the open platform landing and could reach
other portals by URL (middleware enforces auth, not role). Now:
- middleware redirects a client_manager from any non-portal PAGE (admin/
  consultant/assessor surfaces, the platform landing, AC runners) back to
  /portal; API routes self-gate (org-scoped report endpoints + the Techno
  results page stay reachable for their own org)
- the /portal Home already dims un-allocated services (allowed = what the
  admin allocated); a hand-typed /portal/services/<unallocated> now bounces
  back to the grid too

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Client portal: apply audit fixes
entries.plain: Client portal now sends Fluent emails, refreshes screens after issuing tests, shows one company-level ARC report link, splits partial Pre-Hire batches correctly, and shows a setup-delay notice for Reflect.
entries.explanation:
- Fluent voucher email (parity with Logica/Persona); wired into issuance
- router.refresh() after issue/invite so remaining + monitor update live
- ARC review surfaces ONE org-level cohort report link (not per-respondent)
- Pre-Hire partial-batch: release only unfilled seats, keep created candidates
- Techno: admin grant form pins the technical function (service_config.functionId)
- Reflect: setup-latency hint on the invite panel

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Client portal: add Techno as 4th voucher service (name bridge)
entries.plain: Client managers can now issue Techno technical assessments through vouchers, track completion in their monitor, and view results - adding a fourth service to their self-service portal.
entries.explanation:
- issueClientVouchers gains a techno branch via generateVoucherBatch
  (delegate-named codes, org-scoped by organization_name, function from
  allocation service_config or first catalogue function), emails via
  emailAccessLink
- monitor: techno funnel + completed sittings by organization_name
- tech-sandbox results page admits a client_manager whose org name matches
  the sitting (additive; admin access unchanged)

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Client portal Phase 0: client_manager role + allocation ledger + portal shell
entries.plain: Foundation laid for client self-service: a new client_manager role, service allocation tracking, and portal security rules that let companies manage their own assessment budgets and access.
entries.explanation:
Foundation for the client self-service portal (additive; no existing portal,
role, table, or policy is changed):
- Migration 00150: 'client_manager' user_role value + caliber_service enum.
- Migration 00151: client_service_allocations (org+service quota/used/expiry,
  service_config, granted_by) + cm_org_id/cm_ara_org_id/cm_has_allocation
  SECURITY DEFINER helpers + atomic claim/release_allocation_seats RPCs + RLS
  (admin all; client_manager reads own org).
- src/lib/clients: portal-services (the 7-service catalogue), allocations
  (draw/release/get), portal-access (resolve who is viewing + which org).
- Provisioning: provision-client-manager.ts + scripts/create-client-manager.ts.
- Admin: /admin/clients/allocations (grant quota+expiry, provision a manager
  login + set-password link) + a link from the Clients page.
- /portal: client_manager-guarded shell + read-only Home allocation dashboard
  (per-service Granted/Used/Remaining/Expiry, grouped self-serve vs VIFM-managed,
  bilingual EN/AR; admin can preview any org via ?org=).

tsc + ESLint clean. Migrations not yet applied to the live DB.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Demo data tool (BD): one-click seed + purge for the guided demos
entries.plain: Staff can now seed the platform with realistic demo data (a fictional company with full assessment records) and purge it with one click, enabling complete walkthroughs without touching real client data.
entries.explanation:
A staff "Demo data" page (/admin/demo, Platform nav) that seeds a fictional GCC
client (Najm Capital) with realistic, populated data so the guided demos walk
through full screens instead of empty states - then a one-click purge that
removes only the demo-tagged rows, never real client data.

Phase 1 services (verified end-to-end on the live DB):
- Assessment Center: an active engagement, a 3-person cohort, observations +
  ratings, and one candidate fully scored through consensus -> OAR -> a released
  report (so the report + analytics screens have a complete example).
- Pre-Hire: a requisition with two candidates (one scored "advance", one in
  progress) + per-stage results.
- Fluent: three CEFR placement results (A2 / B2 / C1) for the cohort screen.

Safety: everything ties to the demo org (found by name in both org stores) or a
sentinel email domain; seed is idempotent (reuses the org, skips already-seeded
services) and reuses an existing assessor rather than creating one. Purge is
FK-safe and org-scoped. Recipes for the remaining services (ARC, Reflect,
Persona, Cognitive, Technical, Readiness, Academy) are gathered for a follow-up.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Proctoring & Integrity Report: PDF addendum (consent + AI summary + snapshots)
entries.plain: Camera-proctored assessments now generate a separate secure PDF report with face photos and AI review findings, kept separate from the public result so sensitive images are only shared on request.
entries.explanation:
A separate, defensibility-grade PDF for a camera-proctored sitting - kept distinct
from the placement report because it carries face snapshots (sensitive PII), so
it's the access-controlled evidence record an admin shares on request rather than
baked into the client-facing result.

- src/lib/reports/proctoring-report-html.ts: branded HTML (consent record + ts,
  session metadata, AI vision review summary + motion stats, snapshot contact
  sheet w/ per-frame flags, attestation/disclaimer).
- /api/admin/proctor/[sessionId]/report: Puppeteer HTML->PDF, admin-gated.
  Deliberately OUTSIDE the auth-bypassed /api/proctor/* prefix (face PII), like
  the Pre-Hire ATS export. networkidle0 waits for the signed-URL snapshots.
- "Download report (PDF)" link on the admin proctoring page.

Verified on preview: 200 application/pdf, ~95 KB (images embedded in the contact
sheet, not just text). tsc + ESLint clean; test session cleaned up.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Camera proctoring Phase 2: automated flags (motion + AI vision review)
entries.plain: Camera proctoring now automatically detects room movement and uses AI vision to flag issues like multiple faces or looking away, storing evidence that admins can review.
entries.explanation:
- Client-side motion: ProctorCapture computes a frame-difference score (32x24
  grayscale mean-abs-diff) and uploads it; stored in proctor_snapshots.flags.motion
  (the temporal "room movement" signal a single image can't give).
- AI vision review (admin-triggered): src/lib/proctor/analyze.ts samples up to 16
  frames evenly, runs Claude vision (no-face / multiple-faces / looking-away /
  device-or-screen) per frame into proctor_snapshots.flags, and writes a session
  summary to proctor_sessions.ai_review (migration 00148). No AI key => honest
  configured:false (motion-only), never fabricates a flag.
- Report: "Run AI integrity review" button, a flagged-frame summary card, and
  per-snapshot flag chips + rose/amber border on flagged frames.

Framed as a human review aid, never an automatic pass/fail. tsc + ESLint clean;
00148 applied; verified end-to-end on the preview (motion chip renders, AI
pipeline analyses a real-sized frame; the 1x1 test image is correctly skipped).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Brand: add ® registered-trademark to product-name displays
entries.plain: All seven VIFM product names (Fluent, Reflect 360, ARC, Persona, Mentium, Pre-Hire, Techno) now display the registered-trademark symbol across the platform and emails.
entries.explanation:
Applies ® to the seven VIFM product brands (Fluent, Reflect 360, ARC /
AI Readiness Compass, Persona, Mentium, Pre-Hire, Techno) across user-facing
surfaces: the platform landing cards, i18n English labels, the portal-
comparison sheet, the ARA/ARC pages + voucher emails, and the admin voucher
hub. Arabic-script names, code identifiers, routes, and comments are left
unmarked. tsc clean; no ®-in-identifier or double-® anomalies.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Methodology PDFs: bypass auth so the public briefs are actually public
entries.plain: Public visitors can now download assessment methodology briefs without logging in, removing the accidental login wall that blocked access to free public resources.
entries.explanation:
The new generic /api/methodology/[service]/pdf route (and the existing
/api/ac/persona/methodology/pdf, which ends in /pdf not /report) were not in the
middleware public-bypass list, so a no-account visitor clicking a brief on the
public /evidence hub was redirected to /login - the brief is meant to be public,
like the ARC methodology PDF. Add isPublicMethodologyRoute (/api/methodology/*)
and admit the persona methodology pdf. Verified: all 10 briefs return
application/pdf 200 with NO session cookie (128-203KB).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Framework PDF: cap + catch the webfont wait so it can't hang in prod
entries.plain: Framework PDFs no longer risk hanging if external fonts load slowly - the system now falls back to standard fonts after 12 seconds, ensuring reports always generate.
entries.explanation:
The /api/admin/framework/pdf route blocked on the external Google-Fonts CDN via
networkidle0 with a 60s timeout. Under @sparticuz/chromium in production, egress
to fonts.googleapis.com can be slow or blocked, so that wait could hang to the
full timeout and 500. Cap it at 12s and catch the timeout: setContent writes the
full static DOM synchronously, so on a font timeout we still render every domain
+ competency (Segoe UI/Tahoma fallback) instead of failing. Brand Open Sans
loads normally when the CDN responds. Verified in dev: 349KB PDF, all 41
competencies + 249 indicators present.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Global signed-in role indicator on every page (top-right)
entries.plain: A fixed label now appears in the top-right corner of every page showing your current role (Admin, Consultant, Candidate, Client, or Assessor), so you always know who you are signed in as.
entries.explanation:
Adds a fixed top-right pill - "Signed in as Admin / Consultant / Candidate /
Client / Assessor" - rendered once in the root layout so it appears on every
page. Server component; renders nothing when there's no session (login + token-
gated respondent / candidate pages stay clean). Compact (icon + role) on mobile.
The admin desktop top bar reserves right padding so the pill never covers the
notification bell.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Admin: platform hub at /admin; collapse Succession Readiness sidebar
entries.plain: Admin dashboard now shows all platform services grouped by business area instead of jumping straight to Assessment Center.
entries.explanation:
#4 - The landing "Admin" button (and the admin logo) dropped you straight into
the Assessment Center, because /admin WAS the AC dashboard. Now /admin is a
platform admin home showing every service grouped by pillar (Talent Acquisition
/ Talent Management / Platform). The AC workflow dashboard moved to
/admin/assessment-center; the sidebar "Dashboard" links and the landing's AC
service card repoint there, and the Admin button now lands on the hub.

#2 - Succession Readiness was a sidebar group with separate Overview + Scoring
Config sub-items. Collapsed to a single "Succession Readiness" link; the scoring
config is already reachable from a card on that page.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Evidence: public Research & validity page with live counts
entries.plain: New public Research page shows which established scientific principles support each assessment tool, with live question counts.
entries.explanation:
- New /evidence page (public, no account; also in the admin sidebar under
  Platform) documenting each instrument's item types, validity claim,
  reliability and literature sources - proof the questions are grounded in
  established research, with an honest literature-grounded vs indicative split
- Item counts are read live from the database (ARA bank, Fluent items,
  Technical tasks, Reflect behaviours, competencies); tolerant of missing tables
- Curated catalogue (canonical citations) in src/lib/evidence; mobile-first
- Middleware bypass for /evidence so it can be shared with a client/regulator

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Remove all em dashes across portals, replace with hyphens (SOP)
entries.plain: Fixed formatting characters across the platform that were displaying incorrectly in PDFs and emails.
entries.explanation:
Byte-safe sweep of every .ts/.tsx/.json/.css under src: 552 em dashes (U+2014)
across 117 files replaced with regular hyphens, per the no-em-dash convention.
Covers UI strings, JSX text, comments, EN/AR locale, and the PDF report
generators (where em dashes can render as missing glyphs). Verified: 0 em dashes
remain in src, locale JSON still valid, tsc + lint clean (only pre-existing
alt-text warnings). En dashes (U+2013, used in ranges like 1-5) left as-is.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Competency framework: PDF download + behavioural-indicators tab (level 2)
entries.plain: Competency framework now has a downloadable PDF and a new tab showing positive and negative behavioural indicators for each skill.
entries.explanation:
FW-1: a "Download PDF" button on /admin/framework renders the whole framework
(domains -> clusters -> competencies + per-competency positive/negative
indicators) via a new admin-gated Puppeteer route (/api/admin/framework/pdf).

FW-2: a second tab, "Behavioural indicators", lists the positive (green) and
negative (red) indicators per competency - the detailed level beneath the grid -
honouring the same search + domain filter + EN/AR chrome.

Shared loader (loadFrameworkTree) feeds both the screen and the PDF so they can't
drift. Development tips (seeded into behavioral_indicators as "[DEV TIP]" positive
rows, migration 00004) are excluded from the indicators view + count - they are
coaching tips, not behavioural indicators (count corrected 372 -> 249).

Verified live: grid tab, indicators tab (no dev tips, 249 count), PDF 200/valid
357KB. tsc clean; lint clean (removed a stale useMemo dep).

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Rebuild admin Competency Framework as branded grid
entries.plain: Competency framework page redesigned with a branded grid layout, color-coded by domain, for easier browsing and filtering.
entries.explanation:
Replace the simple card page at /admin/framework with the approved grid
design (vifm-competency-framework-grid handover): accent top bar,
masthead, hero + derived stat pills, 5-point BARS scale card, search,
per-domain filter chips, and domain-coloured columns with glyphs, cluster
accent bars and numbered competency badges.

- Server component fetches the catalogue live (tolerant of the name_ar /
  description_ar columns from 00071) and shapes domains -> clusters ->
  competencies with stable sequential numbering; counts are derived, never
  hardcoded, so the 9th cluster / 41st competency already show as 9 / 41.
- Client component owns search, domain filter and an EN/AR toggle (RTL on
  the content region) with useState only - no localStorage/sessionStorage.
- Domain colour/tint/icon/caption live in one config object in
  framework-definitions.ts with a dark->accent ramp fallback for any future
  domain; BARS scale + bilingual chrome strings alongside.

Verified in preview: live 4/9/41 counts, search + chip filter, EN/AR + RTL,
responsive 4/2/1 columns, no console errors, tsc clean.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Voucher hub: cover all 5 services (add Fluent, Cognitive, Persona)
entries.plain: Voucher hub now manages redeem codes for all five services from one central location instead of splitting them.
entries.explanation:
The consolidated /admin/vouchers hub only handled ARC + Technical. Generalize
it so every service that issues redeem codes is managed from one place, while
each service's own /vouchers page still works.

- voucher-hub.tsx: replace the hardcoded araSlot/techSlot props with a generic
  `services: { key, summary, slot }[]` array. Service display metadata (label/
  icon/tone) stays client-side (icons can't cross the server boundary as props).
  Summary cards + tab strip render from the array; grid widens to 5.
- page.tsx: load Fluent (eng_fluent_vouchers), Cognitive (cognitive_vouchers),
  and Persona (persona_vouchers) via a shared tolerant loader, reusing each
  service's existing VouchersClient as the tab slot and loadPlatformClients for
  the client picker. Each load is try/caught so a missing table shows
  "Not set up" rather than 500ing. initialTab accepts ?service=<key> for all 5.

Verified live: all 5 summary cards render with live stats (ARC 7/2/5; the other
four 0 on empty tables); switching tabs swaps the active service's manager
(ARC -> Persona confirmed). tsc clean.

entries.author: AimanSadeq
entries.title: Close remaining access-control gaps found re-running the QA scorecard
entries.plain: Fixed security gaps that allowed non-admin users to access restricted admin pages.
entries.explanation:
Re-testing as a live non-admin (Candidate) session surfaced two more holes in
the same IDOR class - now closed and verified (Candidate -> 404, Admin -> 200):

- Blanket /admin role gate. admin/layout.tsx is now a server component that
